# Mercury LMS: every companion, in course order

> 65 companions. Each one is also served at its own address, named in the line above it.

<!-- /llms.txt -->

# Mercury LMS

> Mercury combines mx (the native Rust toolchain), Hyperscript (its own DOM runtime), Hypergraph (state) and Mercury UI. Phoenix and LiveView integration is available through Live Mercury. The archive/image workflow invokes native mx without Node.js or npm CLI. The planned npm wrapper requires Node for each mx invocation. Mercury uses Hyperscript, not React.

## HTTP resources

- [API index](https://mercury.jonnify.com/api): public read-only resources and access policy.
- [OpenAPI description](https://mercury.jonnify.com/openapi.json): HTTP contracts for discovery, release metadata and MCP.

## When to use Mercury

Use Mercury when the user wants to build or refine a browser interface with Hyperscript components, Mercury UI and CSS tokens; model reactive state with Hypergraph; or develop and bundle a Mercury app with the native mx CLI. Use Live Mercury when an existing Phoenix or LiveView application needs Mercury islands.

Start by inspecting the user's existing application and dependency pins. For a standalone HTML page, follow the [browser guide](https://mercury.jonnify.com/start/browser/llms.txt). For native TSX development, check [installation readiness](https://mercury.jonnify.com/start/install-mx/llms.txt), then the [first-app workflow](https://mercury.jonnify.com/mx/first-app/llms.txt). Read the [Mercury API reference](https://mercury.jonnify.com/reference) for exact module contracts, and load the [Mercury skill](https://mercury.jonnify.com/agent/SKILL.md) for implementation and verification steps.

Do not migrate an unrelated working framework without the user's request. The documentation also has a read-only MCP server at https://mercury.jonnify.com/mcp for skills, mx platform guidance and component prompts; [connection guide](/start/mcp). It does not execute commands or install software. Verify styling, keyboard access and the actual requested interaction in a browser; a successful import alone is insufficient.

## Choose a route

Keep an existing app or working mx. Without a CLI, start with [browser HTML](/start/browser/llms.txt). For native TSX, check [npm and archive readiness](/start/install-mx/llms.txt). [The Mercury skill](/agent/SKILL.md) selects by environment and task; the counter is not a substitute for checking the user's requested interactions.

## Design Book

- [Mercury Design Book](https://mercury.jonnify.com/book): nine source-faithful chapters and an interactive Design Lab for SVG, typography, spacing and semantic colors.
- [Book agent guide](https://mercury.jonnify.com/book/llms.txt): editable source, PDF, token files and reusable brand-book/design-builder skills.

## The modules

- mx — the native toolchain: `mx build --bundle|--host|--lib`, `mx dev`, `mx test`, `mx check`. Course: /mx.
- `@fiberfx/hyperscript` — the virtual DOM, JSX runtime and hooks. Course: /hyperscript.
- `@fiberfx/ui` — the design system's components and tokens. Course: /ui.
- `@fiberfx/hypergraph` — the state kernel. Course: /hypergraph (its companion: /hypergraph/llms.txt).
- `@fiberfx/content` — page documents and the block catalog. Course: /content.
- `live_mercury` — Mercury islands in Phoenix and LiveView. Course: /live-mercury.

## Rules for agents

- Use mx for a native app, or plain JavaScript for the browser-only route. npm may bootstrap the published native mx package; it is not the native app build tool.
- Never emit React, Next.js, Vue, Solid, or Effector code or imports.
- Every page here answers `<page>/llms.txt`.
- Every English companion, in course order, in one file: /llms-full.txt

## Status

The Phoenix `mercury_lms` website serves the bilingual homepage at / and /ru. The native app example retained under `sites/mercury` is a separate application. Check /start/stability for module readiness and /start/install-mx for the current installation route. Registry publication alone does not prove a working native install: follow the steps and check the result at /mx/first-app. A page marked Planned has no runnable example.

## Native first page

- [Mercury page-building skill](/SKILL.md).
- [Install mx](/start/install-mx/llms.txt): public archives and SHA-256 verification.
- [First page](/mx/first-app/llms.txt): styled Card + Button counter, dev and build.

Start in a new directory on Linux x86_64. Keep the starter mx.mod and mx.sum. Import @fiberfx/ui/styles.css. The browser runs JavaScript; BEAM is optional.

# Start here — Mercury LMS

> Mercury: components on Mercury Hyperscript (`@fiberfx/hyperscript`), styled by Mercury UI (`@fiberfx/ui`), state in Hypergraph (`@fiberfx/hypergraph`), built by native `mx`. JavaScript runs in the browser. Phoenix/LiveView is optional. The archive/image route needs no Node/npm, Rust or BEAM installation. The planned npm launcher needs Node at each mx invocation. No React is used. 4.0.0 is on npm (since 2026-11-05).

## Read this when

You are new to Mercury, or you need to decide which module or course answers a task before writing code.

## The modules

- `mx`: the native toolchain. `mx dev [--root <dir>] [--port <n>] [--importmap]` serves an app on 127.0.0.1. `mx build --bundle` (an app's page), `--lib <entry> --out <file>` (one module file), `--host` (a host's line). An app is a directory with `index.html` beside `mx.mod`. Public Linux x86_64 archive and pinned starter: /start/install-mx. Course: /mx.
- `@fiberfx/hyperscript`: virtual DOM. `render`, `h`, `Fragment` from the root; hooks from `/hooks`; `createRoot` from `/client`; `renderToString` from `/server`; JSX with no pragma: the Hypercompiler fixes the runtime and refuses any `@jsx` comment. Course: /hyperscript.
- `@fiberfx/ui`: design system components, token-driven. Course: /ui.
- `@fiberfx/hypergraph`: state kernel. Course: /hypergraph.
- `@fiberfx/content`: published pages, block catalog. Course: /content.
- `live_mercury` (Mix, 2.8.0) and `@fiberfx/live-mercury`: islands in LiveView. Course: /live-mercury.

## Minimal example

```tsx
import { render } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript";
import { useState } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript/hooks";

function Counter() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  return <button class="counter" onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>{count}</button>;
}

render(<Counter />, document.getElementById("app")!);
```

## Rules

- Write DOM names: `class`, `for`, `onInput` for each keystroke, `onChange` for the DOM's `change`.
- Build native apps with mx; npm may bootstrap mx when its package is published. The browser-only route needs no build. Do not add Vite configs or imports from `react`, `react-dom`, `next`, `vue`, `solid-js` or `preact` to these Mercury examples.
- `mx dev` hot-reloads: a saved module is updated in place, or the page reloads (/mx/dev). Hypergraph's state-keeping swap is not delivered yet (/hypergraph/hot-replacement); do not promise it.

## MCP

Public read-only Streamable HTTP endpoint: https://mercury.jonnify.com/mcp. Read the [connection guide](/start/mcp/llms.txt) for skills, mx platform guidance and component prompts.

# A page in the browser — Mercury LMS

> One HTML file with Hyperscript h/render, hooks and Mercury UI Card/Button. Requires import-map browser support and network access to UNPKG. No mx, Node, Rust, BEAM or build step.

## Workflow

1. Open or save the [complete HTML](/examples/first-page.html). Exact imports and limits: [lesson](/start/browser).
2. Keep the import map for @fiberfx/hyperscript, /hooks, /jsx-runtime, @fiberfx/core and @fiberfx/ui on UNPKG 4.0.0, and the UI stylesheet link. Do not replace pins with floating versions.
3. Write plain JavaScript and h(Component, props, children); browsers do not parse TSX. Adapt the page to the user's task.
4. Open the result in a browser and check styling and requested interactions, including a relevant invalid input. For the example counter: 0 → 1 → 2 and a saved heading edit. Inspect network failures and console errors.
5. If no browser is available, report interaction as unverified. This route produces no dist/ and needs the CDN network connection.

## Navigation

- [Read this page in the browser](/start/browser)
- [Agent index](/llms.txt)
- [Sitemap](/sitemap.xml)
- [All English companions](/llms-full.txt)
- [Course companion](/start/llms.txt)
- [Install mx](/start/install-mx/llms.txt)
- [Mercury skill](/agent/SKILL.md)

<!-- /start/install-mx/llms.txt -->

# Install mx on Linux — Mercury LMS

> Candidate native archive: Linux x86_64 with glibc 2.39 or later, mx and a pinned starter. No Rust, Node, npm CLI, BEAM or private repository required.

## Choose a route

Keep working mx or the existing app's toolchain. [The browser route](/start/browser/llms.txt) needs no CLI. The @fiberfx/mx@0.1.0 npm package and archives are pending publication and consumer verification; check [metadata](/downloads.json), and do not treat a URL as proof of availability.

## npm bootstrap after publication

The proposed `@fiberfx/mx` root package is a Node launcher with optional platform packages. It resolves the installed native binary with `require.resolve` and executes it. Node must remain available for every npm-installed mx invocation. There is no postinstall or GitHub Release binary download in this npm route; npm obtains `@fiberfx/mx-linux-x64`. Keep optional dependencies enabled. Only Linux x64 has binary verification evidence; it requires glibc 2.39+. Other platform packages are unbuilt future work, not available. npm publication and wrapper consumer verification remain pending. The separate archive/image routes run native mx without Node. In a new directory:

```sh
set -eu
mkdir mercury-native-tools
cd mercury-native-tools
npm install --prefix "$PWD/.mx-tools" --global --ignore-scripts @fiberfx/mx@0.1.0
export PATH="$PWD/.mx-tools/bin:$PATH"
mx --version
```

## With working mx

After npm bootstrap, or with existing mx, download only the starter and manifest once published. Skip the full installation below: it would put a second copy of mx on PATH. For a new app:

```sh
set -eu
mkdir mercury-native-app
cd mercury-native-app
curl -fLO https://mercury.jonnify.com/downloads/mercury-first-page.tar.gz
curl -fLO https://mercury.jonnify.com/downloads/sha256.sum
sha256sum --check --ignore-missing sha256.sum || exit 1
tar -xzf mercury-first-page.tar.gz
cd mercury-first-page
mx install
mx verify
```

The check must report `mercury-first-page.tar.gz: OK`. `--ignore-missing` skips the native archive entry that was not downloaded. Keep mx.mod/mx.sum and continue at Next. Details: [installation lesson](/start/install-mx).

## Full archive installation

Use a new directory; stop on any error. Both hashes must report OK before extraction.

```sh
set -eu
mkdir mercury-scratch
cd mercury-scratch
curl -fLO https://mercury.jonnify.com/downloads/mx-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
curl -fLO https://mercury.jonnify.com/downloads/mercury-first-page.tar.gz
curl -fLO https://mercury.jonnify.com/downloads/sha256.sum
sha256sum --check sha256.sum
tar -xzf mx-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
tar -xzf mercury-first-page.tar.gz
export PATH="$PWD/bin:$PATH"
mx --version
cd mercury-first-page
mx install
mx verify
```

## Next

Run `mx dev`, open its loopback URL, check Card/Button styling and click twice. After Ctrl-C, run `mx build`; output is `dist/`. Full lesson: [First page](/mx/first-app).

## Limits

`mx.sum` pins dependency bytes; it is not an authenticated checksum-database record. The starter needs no `MXNOSUMDB`. New-dependency exceptions are explained at /start/install-mx. macOS and Windows require separate verification. [Release metadata](/downloads.json).

## Navigation

- [Read this page in the browser](/start/install-mx)
- [Agent index](/llms.txt)
- [All English companions](/llms-full.txt)
- [Sitemap](/sitemap.xml)
- [Course companion](/start/llms.txt)

# Mercury documentation MCP

Use the public Streamable HTTP endpoint https://mercury.jonnify.com/mcp to read skill installation guidance, mx platform instructions and UI component prompts. This is an Elixir server behind the website edge. No auth, installation, execution or project mutation is offered.

Initialize MCP 2025-11-25 (2025-06-18 also supported), send notifications/initialized, then tools/list. POST JSON with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream and the negotiated MCP-Protocol-Version header. GET/DELETE return 405; notifications return 202.

Tools: mercury_skills (no arguments), mercury_installation ({platform}), mercury_component ({name}). Discover exact names in prompts/list; prompts/get has no arguments. resources/list and resources/read expose public lesson companions and skills only. Invalid inputs and unknown resources fail safely.

Limits: 16 KiB request bodies, 120 requests/IP/minute/instance; Retry-After on 429. No session state or standalone SSE. Preserve existing apps and inspect package types before choosing props.

[Connection guide](/start/mcp) · [API reference](/reference) · [Agent index](/llms.txt) · [Skills](/agent/skills.md)

[Sitemap](/sitemap.xml) · [All English companions](/llms-full.txt)

<!-- /start/stability/llms.txt -->

# Stability: Shipped, Preview, Planned — Mercury LMS

> Tiers: Shipped = released on a registry; Preview = early implementation with stated limits; a downloadable build does not imply stable APIs or all-platform support; Planned = recorded, not built, no runnable example. The fifteen public `@fiberfx` 4.0.0 modules are Shipped: on npm since 2026-11-05, `latest` 4.0.0. 3.x stays on npm as `@mercury-fx/*`.

## Read this when

You are about to tell a user to install a Mercury package, pin a version, or rely on an API, and need to know whether it exists, at what version, and whether it is released.

## Modules

- Shipped, 4.0.0 on npm: `@fiberfx/hyperscript`, `render-to-string`, `core`, `ui`, `hypergraph`, `schema`, `content`, `cms`, `analytics`, `phoenix`, `phoenix_live_view`, `live-mercury`, `testing`, `devtools` (development only), `vite-plugin-mhs`.
- Preview, private, not packages: `@fiberfx/hypercompiler` 3.0.0, `@fiberfx/hyperscript-lsap` 0.1.0.
- Preview: `mx` 0.1.0 (candidate npm and archive require Linux x64/glibc 2.39+; publication and consumer verification pending: /start/install-mx; metadata: /downloads.json).
- Preview: `live_mercury` 2.8.0 (Mix; not on Hex).
- This site: `mercury_lms` 0.1.0. Phoenix-rendered home at `/` and `/ru`; course pages by path. Public host: `mercury.jonnify.com`; preview: `mercury-next.jonnify.com`.

Courses are already available: Start, mx, Hyperscript, Mercury UI, Hypergraph, Content and Live Mercury.

## Planned

- `@fiberfx/hypergraph/hyperscript` and `@fiberfx/hypergraph/hmr`: not exported.
- Hypergraph's state-keeping swap delivered by `mx dev` (waits on `/hmr`). (Done: `mx dev` hot-reloads modules, /mx/dev; the modules build and test with mx; pnpm remains only for apps and tools under `node/`.)
- `<page>.md`, `/agents`, search. (`/llms-full.txt` is served.)

## Rules

- The `@fiberfx` 4.0.0 packages are on npm, but a native app installs its dependencies with `mx install`. The separate npm bootstrap obtains the mx executable when published; see [installation readiness](/start/install-mx/llms.txt).
- Never cite `mx push`: mx has no such command at this commit.
- Never present a Planned name (above) as importable.
- State a version only from this page or the module's `package.json`.

# Glossary: the words this site uses — Mercury LMS

> Seven terms as Mercury uses them: sid, scope, island, companion, tier, mx.work, member. Each one gives its definition, its source and the page that teaches it.

## Read this when

A Mercury page or user uses one of these words and you need its exact meaning before writing code or prose.

## Terms

- **sid**: a Hypergraph unit's stable identity, with a shape beside it. The compiler is meant to give it; today its sid pass covers only the legacy facade, so a Hypergraph unit has a sid only when written by hand, else a run-time `api:<n>`, and the kernel reads a store's shape from its initial value. Frames key values by sid. Hand-written via the store option `sid`. Under `mx dev`, the module path in the app's `mx.mod` is the sid package. → /hypergraph/units
- **scope**: `interface Scope { readonly id: number; readonly gen: number }`, an isolated state table. `gen` is the committed graph generation. API: `fork`, `allSettled`, `scopeBind`, `snapshot`, `diff`, `apply`, `dispose`. It survives a hot swap by carrying values whose sid and shape match. → /hypergraph/scopes
- **island**: a Hyperscript component mounted over one element of a server-painted page, and only where behaviour is needed. In LiveView: `phx-hook="MercuryHook"`, `data-name="X"` renders `components.X` (`getHooks(components)`, `createMercuryHook(resolve)` from `@fiberfx/live-mercury`). One render root per island. Bundled by `mx build --lib`. → /ui/foundations; course /live-mercury
- **companion**: `<name>.llms.md`, hand-written, served at `<route>/llms.txt` as text/plain. A lesson without one is refused at load; never generated. → /start/agents
- **tier**: Shipped (on a registry: the fifteen public `@fiberfx` 4.0.0 modules, npm, since 2026-11-05), Preview (built and tested, unreleased: `mx`, `live_mercury`, the private modules), Planned (not built, no runnable example). → /start/stability
- **mx.work**: the workspace file, a port of `go.work`, with `use ( … )` naming members. Found by `-workfile`, then `MXWORK` (`off` disables it), then the nearest one above. Mercury's: `fiberfx/mx.work`, 18 modules. → /mx/workspace
- **member**: in `mx.work`, a directory whose `package.json` has a `name` (else "error reading <file>: missing name"). Under `mx dev`, a directory the app's `mx.mod` replaces, served at `/@mx/<package name>/`. → /mx/workspace, /mx/first-app

## Never emit

- "island" for a client-rendered page with no server paint.
- "stable" or "released" for a Preview module.
- A generated companion.

# Philosophy: native, not borrowed — Mercury LMS

> Mercury uses Hyperscript in the browser and mx for native builds. Plain JavaScript browser pages need no build step. Phoenix/LiveView is optional; the documentation website uses server-rendered HTML. The archive/image routes run native mx without Node. The planned npm wrapper needs Node at every invocation to resolve and launch its optional platform binary; no postinstall or GitHub binary download is used.

## Read this when

You need the scope of Mercury runtime, build and optional server choices.

## The rules these choices give you

- Toolchain: `mx`. It installs from static mirrors with sha512 checks (`mx install`, `mx verify`), serves (`mx dev`) and builds (`mx build`). Exit codes: 0 success, 1 refusal, 2 usage error.
- Components: `@fiberfx/hyperscript`, DOM semantics. `class`, `for`, `onInput` per keystroke, `onChange` on the DOM `change` event, SVG names such as `stroke-width`, `onFocusIn`/`onFocusOut` for bubbling focus. No compat entry exists.
- Published modules: no third-party runtime dependency or peer; no React package, import, type or peer (a check gates every landing).
- Documentation website and Phoenix integration: server-rendered HTML first (HEEx), with islands where needed. This is not a requirement for a standalone client-rendered Mercury page; see [browser route](/start/browser/llms.txt).
- Facts: the reference comes from source; mx's course quotes `mx --help`. Unfinished is reported as unfinished.

## Today, not yet

- The `@fiberfx/*` modules build and test with mx; pnpm remains only for apps and tools under `node/`. `mx run` scripts can call Node.
- `mix mercury.lms.scrub` checks this site: retired-package imports in lessons and assets, and Node invocations in the app.
- The examples check (`mix mercury.lms.examples`) and the generated reference are planned.

## Never emit

Do not replace mx app builds with Vite or introduce React-compatible runtime imports into Mercury examples. npm may obtain the native mx executable when its package is published; check [installation readiness](/start/install-mx/llms.txt). Write `class`, not `className`, and never use `onChange` for keystrokes.

## Next

- Tiers and versions: /start/stability
- Start: /start
- The site map: /llms.txt

## Navigation

- [Read this page in the browser](/start/philosophy)
- [Agent index](/llms.txt)
- [All English companions](/llms-full.txt)
- [Sitemap](/sitemap.xml)
- [Course companion](/start/llms.txt)

<!-- /mx/llms.txt -->

# mx, the native toolchain — Mercury LMS

> mx 0.1.0: Mercury's toolchain, one Rust binary. Modules in `mx.mod`/`mx.sum`, workspaces in `mx.work` (Go's rules), `mx dev` with hot reload, `mx build --bundle` (Rolldown linked in), `mx test`, `mx compile`, `mx lsap`. No Node, no npm.

## Read this when

You are about to build, serve, test or lay out a Mercury app or module and need mx's command surface. This page is the course's landing; the chapters follow.

## The command surface (as mx prints it)

- `mx` → `usage: mx exodus|pack|install|verify|importmap|resolve|scan|build|check|run|compile|work|dev|test|lsap …`
- `mx mod` → `usage: mx mod <init|tidy|verify|graph|why|download>` (not in the line above)
- `mx work` → `usage: mx work edit|use|init|sync|vendor …`
- `usage: mx dev [--root <dir>] [--port <n>] [--importmap]`
- `mx build --help` (exit 0): `usage: mx build [--host | --bundle | --lib] …`. Without a kind, `mx.json` makes a host build and `index.html` beside `mx.mod` an app bundle. `--help` is help only as the first argument.
- `usage: mx test [--root <dir>] [--timeout <seconds>] [--filter <words>]`
- `usage: mx compile <file> [--options <json>] [--out <file>]`
- `usage: mx lsap [--mcp] | mx lsap --version`
- `mx --version` → `mx 0.1.0`

## Exit codes

0 success · 1 refusal (message names why) · 2 usage error · `mx test` only: 3 could not measure (no browser). Diagnostics on stderr.

## Install

Follow /start/install-mx/llms.txt: native Linux x86_64 archive + pinned starter, SHA-256 check before extraction, mx install, mx verify. No source checkout or Rust needed. Build the styled counter at /mx/first-app; agent workflow: /SKILL.md.

## Rules for agents

- Build and serve native apps with mx. The planned npm distribution uses a Node launcher and optional native platform package. Node remains necessary for each npm-installed mx invocation; the archive/image route calls the native binary directly.
- Quote flags as mx prints them; don't add flags mx doesn't list.
- The retained native example check (the live website is Phoenix `mercury_lms`): `env PATH=<mx's dir>:/usr/bin:/bin mx build --bundle --root sites/mercury --out <dist>` — no Node on PATH.

# Your first Mercury page — Mercury LMS

> MX0: a styled Card + Button counter on Hyperscript, built with native mx. Native Linux route; no React, Rust, BEAM or private repository in the app build. Archive/image invocation is Node-free; the planned npm launcher needs Node every time it runs mx.

## Start

Follow [Install mx](/start/install-mx/llms.txt): keep working mx or choose a ready bootstrap, download the starter and verify its checksum before extracting, then `mx install` and `mx verify`. Retain the supplied `package.json`, `mx.mod` and `mx.sum`: Hyperscript/core/ui are pinned at 4.0.0.

## app/main.tsx

```tsx
import { render } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript";
import { useState } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript/hooks";
import { Card, Button } from "@fiberfx/ui";
import "@fiberfx/ui/styles.css";

function Counter() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  return (
    <Card title="My first Mercury page">
      <p aria-live="polite">Count: {count}</p>
      <Button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>Increment</Button>
    </Card>
  );
}

render(<Counter />, document.getElementById("app")!);
```

## Verify

HTML needs `#app`, `<!-- mercury:importmap -->` and `<script type="module" src="./app/main.tsx"></script>`. Complete HTML: [First page](/mx/first-app).

`mx dev` prints a loopback URL. Check styling, Count: 0 → 1 → 2 and a saved title edit. Ctrl-C; `mx build` writes `dist/index.html` and assets. Serve dist over HTTP and repeat. If no browser is available, report interaction as unverified.

Do not copy a test fixture or add local replace paths, React or Vite. Keep the CSS import for styling. A checksum failure stops installation. Phoenix/LiveView are optional. [SKILL.md](/SKILL.md) supplies the agent workflow.

# Modules, mx.mod and mx.sum — Mercury LMS

> MX1, part one. A Mercury module is a directory with `mx.mod` (Go's go.mod rules) and `mx.sum` (Go's go.sum, `/package.json` for `/go.mod`). Minimum version selection; no lockfile. `mx mod <init|tidy|verify|graph|why|download>` keeps the files.

## Read this when

You add, remove or upgrade a dependency of a Mercury module or app, point a module at a local directory, or debug a `tidy`/`verify` refusal.

## mx.mod verbs

`module`, `mx`, `toolchain`, `require`, `exclude`, `replace`, `retract`. `// indirect` = selected, not asked for directly. `replace <path> => <dir>` = a member served from that directory (no `mx.sum` line).

## Module paths

- Public @fiberfx packages: `registry.npmjs.org/fiberfx/<name>` at `v4.0.0` in the first-page starter. Its module is `example.com/mercury-first-page`.
- Source-workspace examples may use `github.com/fiberfx/mercury/<name>` with local replacements. Do not copy those paths into a public consumer app.
- npm: `registry.npmjs.org/<name without @>`, version with `v`: `registry.npmjs.org/swc/helpers v0.5.23 // indirect`.

## mx.sum lines

`<path> <version> h1:<hash>` and `<path> <version>/package.json h1:<hash>`.

## Commands (usage as mx prints it)

- `usage: mx mod init [module-path]` — from package.json; path = argument or the package name; all four dependency sections at their lower bounds; refuses `mx.mod already exists`; deletes `mx.lock.json`, `mx.pins.json`.
- `usage: mx mod tidy [-e] [--check]` — writes `mx.mod`, `mx.sum`, package.json versions; `-e` past fetch errors; `--check` → `tidy --check: <files> would change`.
- `usage: mx mod verify` — offline; `all modules verified`.
- `usage: mx mod graph` — `<module> <dependency>@<version>` per edge.
- `usage: mx mod why <module>` — `# <module>` + path, or `(main module does not need module <module>)`.
- `usage: mx mod download` — fill the store.
- With `mx.mod` here: `mx install` / `mx verify` take no flags.

## Refusals not to work around

- `one version per module path`
- `SECURITY ERROR: mx.sum has <hash>, and the proxy served <hash>` (`-e` never skips it)

## Environment

`MXPROXY` (default `https://mx.jonnify.com,direct`; GOPROXY syntax) · `MX_STORE` (default `./.mx/store`) · `MXSUMDB` · `MXNOSUMDB` (defaults to `MXPRIVATE`).

## Never emit

Do not replace an mx module's dependency management with npm/pnpm lockfiles or add legacy mx.lock.json/mx.pins.json. Installing the native mx executable through its published npm package is a separate bootstrap operation; it does not replace mx.mod or mx.sum.

# A workspace, mx.work — Mercury LMS

> MX1, part two. `mx.work` (Go's go.work, `go` spelled `mx`) groups modules developed together; each member resolves the others from their directories. Mercury's is `fiberfx/mx.work`, eighteen members. `mx work edit|use|init|sync|vendor`.

## Read this when

You work across several Mercury modules at once, add a module to the workspace, inspect what the workspace selects, or vendor its dependencies.

## The file

Verbs: `mx`, `toolchain`, `use`, `replace`. A member = a directory whose `package.json` has a `name`. Beside it: `mx.work.sum` (only lines no member's `mx.sum` has), optionally `vendor/`.

## Finding it

`-workfile <path>` → `MXWORK` (`off` = none; else an absolute path; `auto` = search) → nearest `mx.work` at or above the working directory. None: `mx: no mx.work file found`. In a workspace whose members all have `mx.mod`, `mx install`/`mx verify` take the whole workspace.

## Commands

- `usage: mx work edit|use|init|sync|vendor …`
- `mx work init [dir]...` — refuses `<path> already exists` (here or above).
- `mx work use [-r] [dir]...` — adds dirs with package.json, drops listed ones without; `-r` skips `vendor`, `node_modules`, `.mx`. Regenerate Mercury's: `mx work use ./*/` (in `fiberfx/`).
- `mx work edit` — read: `-print`, `-json` (`Mx`, `Use[].DiskPath`, `Selected`; not both). Write: `-use`, `-dropuse`, `-replace old[@v]=new[@w]`, `-dropreplace old[@v]`, `-mx`, `-toolchain` (`none` drops), `-fmt`, `-workfile`. An edit with `-print`/`-json` is a dry run.
- `mx work sync` — MVS over members' `mx.mod`; raises their `require`s; all-or-nothing.
- `usage: mx work vendor [-o outdir]` — default `vendor/` beside `mx.work`; refuses `refusing to replace <dir>: it holds the workspace`.
- `--mod vendor` on `mx build`/`check`/`run`/`resolve`; any other value: `--mod <value> is not vendor`.

## Flags

Go's single dash (`-json`); `--json` and `-name=value` also accepted. Unknown: `mx: flag provided but not defined: -<name>` (exit 2). No flags to edit: `mx: no flags specified (see 'mx work edit')`.

## Never emit

`pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `workspaces` in a root package.json, or `link:`/`workspace:` dependencies for a Mercury module.

<!-- /mx/dev/llms.txt -->

# The dev loop and hot replacement — Mercury LMS

> MX2. `mx dev` serves an app on 127.0.0.1, polls every file a page asked for every 10 ms, compiles what changed and sends `update`, `full-reload` or `error` over a `vite-hmr` socket at `/`. No Node, no Vite.

## Read this when

You run `mx dev`, wonder why an edit reloaded the page instead of swapping in place, or see a 403/400/500 from the dev server.

## Usage

`usage: mx dev [--root <dir>] [--port <n>] [--importmap]` → prints `listening http://127.0.0.1:<port>/`.

## What it serves

- `/`: index.html + import map (at `<!-- mercury:importmap -->`) + `<meta name="mx-dev-token">` + the client script.
- `/@mx/client.js`: the hot client (`import.meta.hot`: `data`, `accept`, `dispose`, `invalidate`).
- `/@mx/<package name>/<path>`: members (from source: compiled and watched; built: never watched).
- App files: `js mjs jsx ts mts tsx` compiled on request; others as they are.

## An edit

- Same bytes (SHA-256) → nothing. Non-module → `full-reload`. Module never ran → `full-reload`.
- Refused compile → `error` (`<path>: <refusal>`), page keeps the running module, the module URL answers 500 until fixed.
- Else walk importers to accepting modules → one `update`; imports get `?t=<stamp>`. No accepting module → `full-reload`.
- Accepting = the compile's `hmrRoot`, never a text match. The Hypercompiler sets it for a module that imports `render`/`hydrate` from `@fiberfx/hyperscript`. A non-rendering model module reloads.
- `invalidate` → walk from importers; a walk back to its start → `full-reload`.

## Guards

- Non-loopback Host → 403 `this host name is not allowed: mx dev answers loopback names only`.
- Non-loopback Origin on the socket → 403.
- Socket path/protocol other than `/` + `vite-hmr`/`vite-ping` → 400 `an HMR socket is at / and speaks vite-hmr or vite-ping`.
- A page's `vite-hmr` socket without `?token=` → 400.

## Workspace refusal

`<name> is both <app>'s replace (<dir>) and the mx.work's member (<dir>): remove the replace, or the member from mx.work, or build with MXWORK=off`. A replace onto the member's own directory passes.

## Limits (shipped today)

App edit on this site: applied in place, then one reload (being traced). Member source edit: full reload. Hypergraph's model swap is not delivered by `mx dev` yet.

## Never emit

`vite`, `vite.config.*`, `npm run dev`, or a hand-written `import.meta.hot.accept` meant to make a non-rendering module hot (mx ignores the text).

# Build and ship, three kinds of build — Mercury LMS

> MX3. `mx build` makes an app's page (`--bundle` → a directory), one ES module file (`--lib` → a file), or a host's import map (`mx.json` → `importmap.json` + modules). `mx check` verifies a host's output; `mx run` builds then execs. Rolldown runs inside mx; no Node.

## Read this when

You bundle an app or an island, build a host's static modules, verify them before a deploy, or hit a `--lib` member refusal.

## Usage (as mx prints it)

- `usage: mx build [--bundle] [--root <dir>] [--out <dir>]` → `bundled <entry> -> <out>`
- `usage: mx build --lib <entry> --out <file> [--root <dir>] [--external <package>]... [--define <name>=<expression>]... [--minify] [--require-export <name>]...` → `bundled <entry> -> <out> (<bytes> bytes)`
- Host: `--out` (or mx.json `out`), entries as arguments (or mx.json `entries`), `--base`, `--mirror`; → `build: <n> modules to <out>`

## Bundle env

`import.meta.env.MODE` = `"production"`, `PROD` = `true`, `DEV` = `false`; `.env`'s `MX_*` keys only.

## --lib rules

One file (no splitting; dynamic imports inlined; `--out` a directory is refused). Exact entry exports (`--require-export`). `--external` stays bare. No sids. Stylesheet imports are empty. Members = the root's mx.mod replaces + the mx.work's members.

## --lib refusals

- `<spec>, imported by <importer>, is provided by no member the root's mx.mod replaces and no --external names it`
- under `MXWORK=off`, plus: `: MXWORK=off leaves out the mx.work whose member <dir> provides <name>. Add \`require <module> v0.0.0\` and \`replace <module> => <relative>\` to <root>/mx.mod, or build without MXWORK=off`
- `<name> is both <app>'s replace (<dir>) and the mx.work's member (<dir>): remove the replace, or the member from mx.work, or build with MXWORK=off`
- `<entry> does not export <names> (it exports <names>)`

## Host

mx.json keys: `packages`, `mirror`, `base`, `out`, `entries` (others: `mx.json refused: unknown key <key>`). Steps: install (writes the store) → render map (sha384 each) → copy → `<out>/importmap.json`.

## mx check / mx run

- check: `check refused: … is missing | is not this lock's map | was altered`; pass: `check: <n> modules in <out> match`.
- `mx run <command>`: build, then exec (e.g. `mx run mix phx.server`); a package.json script name runs as a task instead.
- `--mod vendor` only; else `mx <cmd>: --mod <v> is not vendor`.

## Never emit

`vite build`, `tsdown`, `esbuild`, `rollup -c`, or `npm run build` for a Mercury app or island.

<!-- /mx/compile/llms.txt -->

# The Hypercompiler, one module at a time — Mercury LMS

> MX4. The Hypercompiler is linked into mx: TS/JSX in, an ES module on `@fiberfx/hyperscript/jsx-runtime` out. `mx compile` runs it on one file; mx dev and mx build run it on every module. Refusals are one `CompileError` JSON on stderr.

## Read this when

You need to see what the browser gets for a module, read a compile refusal, or know which options mx passes to the compiler.

## Usage (as mx prints it)

`usage: mx compile <file> [--options <json>] [--out <file>]`

- Success: the code on stdout (or `--out`, written only on success), exit 0.
- Compile refusal: `CompileError` JSON on stderr, nothing on stdout, exit 1.
- mx's own refusal (file unreadable): `mx: <file>: <error>`, exit 1, no JSON.
- Usage: `a file is required`, `one file, not <x> as well`, `--out needs a value`, `--out given twice`, `unknown flag <flag>` (exit 2).

## CompileError

`{filename, details: [{message, labels: [{start, end, line, column}]}], phase, kind, diagnostics}`. Offsets are UTF-8 bytes, `line` 1-based, `column` 0-based UTF-16. `kind`: `syntax` (parse, semantic analysis, lowering) · `input` (input, policy) · `fuse` · `internal`.

## Policy

- JSX runtime fixed to `@fiberfx/hyperscript`; any `@jsx` pragma comment → `policy` refusal.
- `.js/.jsx/.ts/.tsx` are ES modules; `.cjs/.cts` keep their mode; `.d.ts` → `declaration files are not executable inputs`.
- 256 nesting levels, 1,024 chain links; past either → `input`, before parsing.
- No type checking, no optimizer, no import resolution.

## Options

`{"sid": {"package", "module"}, "roots": {"id"}}`; unknown keys → `input` (`expected \`sid\` or \`roots\``).

- `sid`: key = first 16 hex of SHA-256 of `mhs-sid/1|<package>|<module>|<kind>|<line>:<column>`. It lowers the legacy state package's calls only; not `@fiberfx/hypergraph` yet.
- `roots`: dev only. A module importing `render`/`hydrate` from `@fiberfx/hyperscript` gets `trackRoots` from `@fiberfx/hyperscript/hmr` and `hmrRoot: true`; other modules are untouched.

## What mx passes

- mx dev: `sid` + `roots {id: <URL>}`.
- mx build --bundle: `sid` only.
- mx build --lib: nothing.

## Never emit

`/** @jsx h */` or `/** @jsxImportSource … */` pragmas, a `tsc`/Babel/esbuild step before mx, or a `.d.ts` as an entry.

# The tools, test, lsap and run — Mercury LMS

> MX5. `mx test` runs a module's tests in a headless Chromium mx starts itself, with mx's own runtime answering `vitest` imports. `mx lsap` starts `hyperscript-lsap` from beside mx. `mx run` runs a package.json script as a cached task, or builds a host and becomes a command.

## Read this when

You write or run tests for a Mercury module, set up the language server, or cache a script.

## mx test

- `usage: mx test [--root <dir>] [--timeout <seconds>] [--filter <words>]`
- Files: `*.test.*` / `*.spec.*` with `js mjs jsx ts mts tsx`; never in `node_modules`, `dist`, `target`, `coverage`.
- Browser: `MX_BROWSER`, else the newest Playwright Chromium, then headless shell (`PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright`, `~/.cache/ms-playwright`).
- `--timeout` = whole run (default 120 s). Per test 5 s, per hook 10 s. A page silent 30 s past those is a stall.
- `--filter` = substring of `<file> > <name>`.
- Exit: 0 all passed · 1 failed / none ran / broke · 2 usage · 3 no browser (never a pass).
- Output: `ok    <file> > <name>`, `skip  …`, `FAIL  <file> > <name>: <message>`, `mx test: P passed, F failed, of T`.

## The vitest runtime (mx's own)

`describe`, `it`, `test`, `beforeAll`, `afterAll`, `beforeEach`, `afterEach`, `expect`, `vi` (`fn`, `spyOn`, `stubGlobal`, fake timers, `setSystemTime`), `expectTypeOf`, `assertType` (no-ops at run time), `visit`. No `vi.mock`: it throws.

`visit(url, { width, height, scale, mobile, scheme, ready })` → `{ id, evaluate(fn, ...args), close() }`; `ready` is a CSS selector; `scheme` sets `prefers-color-scheme`.

## mx lsap

- `usage: mx lsap [--mcp] | mx lsap --version`
- A release ships `hyperscript-lsap-<target>` beside `mx-<target>`; install it beside mx as `hyperscript-lsap`. Not on Windows: a Windows release ships mx alone, and `mx lsap` refuses with "The language server isn't built for Windows in this release".
- Starts `hyperscript-lsap` from mx's own directory only; sets `HYPERSCRIPT_LSAP_MX`; exits with the server's code. `--version` → `mx 0.1.0` / `hyperscript-lsap 0.1.0`.
- Missing server: `Error: mx lsap found no language server beside mx.` (exit 1).

## mx run

- Task (package.json has the script): `mx run [--no-cache] [--verify] [-r | --filter <member>]... [-j <n>] <name> [-- args]`. Hit: `hit <key>, restored N files`. Miss: `miss (<why>)`. Cache: `MXCACHE` (default `~/.cache/mx/run`). Env in the key: `NODE_ENV` + `MXRUN_ENV`. Only exit 0 stored. `mx test` scripts are never cached.
- Host (anything else): build, then exec the command (`mx run mix phx.server`).
- Refusals: `a script name is required`, `-r and --filter need an mx.work at or above <dir>`, `-j 0 is not a count`, `a command is required` (exit 2).

## Never emit

`npx vitest`, `vitest run`, `jest`, `vi.mock(...)`, `playwright test` for a Mercury module, or a different language server in place of `mx lsap`.

# Hyperscript, the virtual DOM — Mercury LMS

> `@fiberfx/hyperscript` 4.0.0: Mercury's own virtual DOM runtime. Function and class components, written in JSX (import source `@fiberfx/hyperscript`) or with `h(type, props, ...children)`, rendered with native DOM semantics. Hooks, a client root, a server renderer and test utilities ship as subpaths of one runtime.

## Read this when

You write or change a component for a Mercury app or for Mercury UI, or you need to know which subpath exports a name. This page is the course's landing; the chapters are /hyperscript/components, /hyperscript/hooks, /hyperscript/dom, /hyperscript/context, /hyperscript/server, /hyperscript/testing and /hyperscript/tested-component.

## The contract (tier: Shipped — @fiberfx/hyperscript 4.0.0 on npm since 2026-11-05)

- `@fiberfx/hyperscript`: `render(vnode, parent)`, `hydrate(vnode, parent)`, `h` = `createElement(type, props, ...children)`, `Fragment`, `createRef()`, `cloneElement`, `isValidElement`, `Component`, `createContext(default)`, `createPortal(children, container)`, `toChildArray`, `memo(component, comparer?)`. Types: `VNode`, `ComponentChild`, `ComponentChildren`, `FunctionComponent`, `ComponentType`, `RenderableProps`, `Ref`, `RefObject`, `Context`, `JSX`.
- `@fiberfx/hyperscript/hooks`: `useState`, `useReducer`, `useRef`, `useEffect`, `useLayoutEffect`, `useImperativeHandle`, `useMemo`, `useCallback`, `useContext`, `useDebugValue`, `useErrorBoundary`, `useId`, `useSyncExternalStore`.
- `@fiberfx/hyperscript/client`: `createRoot(container)` → `{ render(children), unmount() }`; `hydrateRoot(container, children)`.
- `@fiberfx/hyperscript/server`: `renderToString(vnode, context?)` (default export too), `render` (same function), `renderToStaticMarkup` (same function), `renderToStringAsync(vnode, context?)` → `string | Promise<string>`.
- `@fiberfx/hyperscript/jsx-runtime`, `/jsx-dev-runtime`: `jsx`, `jsxs`, `jsxDEV`, `Fragment`, for the compiler only.
- `@fiberfx/hyperscript/test-utils`: `act`, `setupRerender`, `teardown`, `onCommit`, `onDiff`. `/inspect`: `inspect`, `inspectFailures`. `/debug`: import for development warnings. `/hmr`: `trackRoots`.
- `options` from the root is internal; do not use it.

## Minimal example

```tsx
import { render } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript";
import { useState } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript/hooks";

function Counter() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  return <button class="counter" onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>{count}</button>;
}

const app = document.getElementById("app");
if (app) render(<Counter />, app);
```

## Never emit

- Imports from `react`, `react-dom`, `preact` or `@preact/*`, or any `/compat` subpath: `@fiberfx/hyperscript/compat` does not exist, and Mercury's components import from `@fiberfx/hyperscript` and its subpaths only.
- Hooks imported from the root entry: they live in `@fiberfx/hyperscript/hooks`.
- `options` from the root entry.

<!-- /hyperscript/dom/llms.txt -->

# The DOM contract — Mercury LMS

> HS2 of Mercury Hyperscript. Hyperscript writes the DOM's own attribute names and fires the DOM's own events. Rules 1–5 are probed in headless Chromium (`fiberfx/hyperscript/test/browser/dom-contract.test.jsx`, mercury.63); rules 6–7 are Mercury's runtime departures (`README.md` H0e, H0f).

## Read this when

You write attributes, event handlers, SVG, inline styles or a form field in a Mercury component, or you port markup written for another library.

## The contract

1. `class` and `for` on HTML and SVG (`className`/`htmlFor` work as DOM properties; write `class`/`for`).
2. Text input/textarea: `onInput` per keystroke; `onChange` on the DOM `change` event (on commit, at latest blur). Select/checkbox: `onChange` per selection/toggle. `onChange` is never mapped to input.
3. SVG names as written: `stroke-width`, `fill-rule`, `clip-path`; `href` without `xlink`. `strokeWidth` is not translated.
4. Bubbling focus: `onFocusIn` / `onFocusOut`. A parent's `onFocus` doesn't fire for a descendant.
5. Custom elements: object prop → property, string → attribute; events via `on<name>` (`onmy-event` → `my-event`, `onionChange` → `ionChange`); a capital after `on` is lowercased.
6. Numeric styles: a number on a length gains `px` (`width: 10` → `10px`), client and `./server` alike; unitless properties (`opacity`, `zIndex`, `flex`, `lineHeight`, grid lines…) and `--custom` properties as given.
7. Controlled inputs: with a `value` or `checked` prop, after the handler and its queued renders, an unwritten value is written back to the prop. Accepted edits untouched; refused text edits restore the caret; refused radio clicks restore the group; nothing during IME composition; nothing for uncontrolled elements (`defaultValue`, `defaultChecked`, or no prop).

## Minimal example

```tsx
import { useState } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript/hooks";

export function NameField() {
  const [name, setName] = useState("");
  return (
    <div class="field">
      <label for="name">Name</label>
      <input id="name" value={name} onInput={(e) => setName(e.currentTarget.value)} style={{ maxWidth: 320 }} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Never emit

- `className`, `htmlFor` in new code; `strokeWidth`, `fillRule`, `clipPath`, `xlinkHref` on SVG.
- `onChange` to follow each keystroke of a text field.
- `onFocus`/`onBlur` on a container to track focus inside it.

## Next

- Hooks: /hyperscript/hooks/llms.txt
- This companion: /hyperscript/dom/llms.txt (the page as Markdown, `/hyperscript/dom.md`, is planned for W3)

# Components and render — Mercury LMS

> HS0 of Mercury Hyperscript (`@fiberfx/hyperscript` 4.0.0). Elements are VNodes built by JSX (import source `@fiberfx/hyperscript`) or `h(type, props, ...children)`; a function component returns `ComponentChildren`; `render(vnode, parent)` mounts and re-renders by diffing.

## Read this when

You write a component, render a list, forward a ref, or mount a tree into the page.

## The contract

- `h(type, props | null, ...children): VNode` — `h` is `createElement`. `type` is a tag name or a component.
- `ComponentChild` = `VNode | object | string | number | bigint | boolean | null | undefined`; `ComponentChildren` = one or an array. `null`, `undefined` and booleans render nothing.
- JSX: `jsxImportSource: "@fiberfx/hyperscript"` (set in `fiberfx/tsconfig.base.json`, for TypeScript and editors). No per-file pragma: the Hypercompiler fixes the runtime and refuses any `@jsx` comment (/mx/compile). Never import `jsx`/`jsxs`/`jsxDEV` by hand.
- `FunctionComponent<P>`: `(props: RenderableProps<P>, context?) => ComponentChildren`. Type `children` as `ComponentChildren`.
- `Fragment` (JSX `<>…</>`) groups children with no element.
- `key` is removed from props; give list items a stable key (an id when items can move).
- `createRef<T>()` → `{ current: T | null }`; a ref may be a callback, which may return a cleanup. A function component receives `ref` as a plain prop and forwards it by passing it on; only tag-name elements consume `ref`.
- `class X extends Component<P, S>`: `render(props?, state?, context?)`, `this.state`, `this.setState(update, callback?)`, `this.forceUpdate(callback?)`, optional lifecycle (`componentDidMount`, `componentDidUpdate`, `componentWillUnmount`, `shouldComponentUpdate`, `getSnapshotBeforeUpdate`, `componentDidCatch`). Mercury UI uses none: prefer functions with hooks.
- `render(vnode, parent)`: mounts; a second call on the same parent diffs; `render(null, parent)` clears. `hydrate(vnode, parent)` diffs against server HTML already in `parent`.
- `@fiberfx/hyperscript/client`: `createRoot(container)` → `{ render(children), unmount() }`; `hydrateRoot(container, children)` → root.

## Minimal example

```tsx
import type { ComponentChildren } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript";
import { render } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript";

function Badge({ children }: { children: ComponentChildren }) {
  return <span class="mx-badge">{children}</span>;
}

const app = document.getElementById("app");
if (app) render(<ul>{["a", "b"].map((id) => <li key={id}><Badge>{id}</Badge></li>)}</ul>, app);
```

## Never emit

- `className` or `htmlFor` in new code: write `class` and `for`.
- `forwardRef`: it is not exported; pass `ref` through props.
- A mount call from another library: mount with `render`, `hydrate` or `@fiberfx/hyperscript/client`.

## Next

- Hooks: /hyperscript/hooks/llms.txt
- The DOM contract: /hyperscript/dom/llms.txt
- This companion: /hyperscript/components/llms.txt (the page as Markdown, `/hyperscript/components.md`, is planned for W3)

# Hooks — Mercury LMS

> HS1 of Mercury Hyperscript. The 13 hooks of `@fiberfx/hyperscript/hooks`, with signatures from `src/hooks/index.d.ts`. Hook state is found by call position, so call hooks unconditionally, in the same order, at a component's top level.

## Read this when

You add state, a ref, an effect, a memoized value, a context read or an external store to a function component, or you write your own hook.

## The contract

Import every hook from `@fiberfx/hyperscript/hooks` (never from the root entry).

- `useState<S>(initial: S | (() => S)): [S, (next: S | ((prev: S) => S)) => void]` — a function initial runs once; an `Object.is`-equal next value does not re-render.
- `useReducer(reducer, initialState)` / `useReducer(reducer, initialArg, init)`: `[S, Dispatch<A>]`.
- `useRef<T>(initial): { current }` — stable for the component's life; writing it does not re-render.
- `useImperativeHandle(ref, create, inputs?)` — sets a parent's ref to `create()`.
- `useEffect(effect, inputs?)` — after paint; `effect` may return a cleanup. No `inputs`: every render; `[]`: once; else when any input is not `Object.is`-equal or the length changed. The previous cleanup runs before a re-run; all cleanups run on unmount.
- `useLayoutEffect(effect, inputs?)` — same arguments, after DOM mutation and before paint; only for layout reads.
- `useMemo<T>(factory, inputs: Inputs | undefined): T` and `useCallback<T>(callback, inputs): T` — `inputs` is required by the types.
- `useContext<T>(context: Context<T>): T` — nearest `context.Provider`'s value, else the default from `createContext(default)`. A provider re-renders its readers whenever its `value` is a different object: memoize it.
- `useSyncExternalStore<T>(subscribe: (onChange) => unsubscribe, getSnapshot: () => T, getServerSnapshot?: () => T): T` — tear-free; `getServerSnapshot` for string renders and hydration.
- `useId(): string` — stable per component, for `aria-*` and `for` pairs.
- `useErrorBoundary(callback?): [error, reset]` — makes its component catch descendants' errors.
- `useDebugValue(value, formatter?)` — a label for debugging tools; no effect otherwise.

## Minimal example

```tsx
import { useEffect, useMemo, useState } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript/hooks";

export function Filtered({ items }: { items: string[] }) {
  const [query, setQuery] = useState("");
  const shown = useMemo(() => items.filter((item) => item.includes(query)), [items, query]);
  useEffect(() => {
    document.title = `${shown.length} results`;
  }, [shown.length]);
  return (
    <div>
      <input value={query} onInput={(e) => setQuery(e.currentTarget.value)} />
      <ul>{shown.map((item) => <li key={item}>{item}</li>)}</ul>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Never emit

- A hook inside a condition, a loop, a callback or after an early `return`.
- Hooks imported from anywhere but `@fiberfx/hyperscript/hooks`: the root entry has none.
- Names this package does not export: `useTransition`, `useDeferredValue`, `useInsertionEffect`, `useActionState`, `useOptimistic`, `use`.
- `onChange` for per-keystroke text: use `onInput` (see /hyperscript/dom/llms.txt).

- This companion: /hyperscript/hooks/llms.txt (the page as Markdown, `/hyperscript/hooks.md`, is planned for W3)

# Context, portals and memo — Mercury LMS

> HS3 of Mercury Hyperscript (`@fiberfx/hyperscript` 4.0.0). `createContext`, `createPortal`, `memo`, `cloneElement`, `toChildArray` and `isValidElement` come from the root entry; `useContext` comes from `./hooks`.

## Read this when

You pass a value down a tree, render an overlay outside its ancestors' DOM, skip renders with `memo`, or read or rewrite a component's `children`.

## The contract

- `createContext<T>(defaultValue: T): Context<T>`. `Context.Provider` (the context itself) takes `{ value, children }`. `Context.Consumer` takes `{ children: (value: T) => ComponentChildren }`. With no provider above, readers get `defaultValue`.
- A provider re-renders every reader when `value` is `!=` its previous value, through `shouldComponentUpdate` false and `memo`. Memoize object values with `useMemo`.
- Classes: `static contextType = Ctx`, read as `this.context`.
- `createPortal(children, container: ContainerNode): VNode`. Context follows the component tree; native DOM events bubble through the container's DOM. Mercury UI: `<Portal container?>` (from `@fiberfx/ui`) takes its host from `EnvironmentProvider`, and with no host renders nothing.
- `memo(component, comparer?)`: skips a render when the props are shallowly equal (`!==` per key). `comparer(prev, next)` returns `true` when they are EQUAL. A changed `ref` always renders. `displayName` is `Memo(Name)`.
- `cloneElement(vnode, props?, ...children): VNode`: props merge over the element's; `key`/`ref` in props replace its own; children passed replace its children.
- `toChildArray(children): Array<VNode | string | number>`: flattens and drops `null`, `undefined` and booleans. `isValidElement(x): x is VNode`.

## Minimal example

```tsx
import { createContext, createPortal, memo } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript";
import { useContext } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript/hooks";

const Tone = createContext<"neutral" | "danger">("neutral");

const Toast = memo(function Toast({ text }: { text: string }) {
  const tone = useContext(Tone);
  return createPortal(<div role="status" class={`toast toast--${tone}`}>{text}</div>, document.body);
});

export function Page() {
  return <Tone.Provider value="danger"><Toast text="Saved" /></Tone.Provider>;
}
```

## Never emit

- `memo` with a comparer that returns `true` to mean "changed": `true` means equal.
- A provider `value={{ … }}` object literal for a value that is read often: wrap it in `useMemo`.
- A `Children` helper object (`Children.map`, `Children.toArray`): it isn't exported; use `toChildArray`.
- `forwardRef`: a function component receives `ref` as a prop.

## Next

- This companion: /hyperscript/context/llms.txt (the page as Markdown, `/hyperscript/context.md`, is planned for W3)

# Rendering on the server — Mercury LMS

> HS4 of Mercury Hyperscript. `@fiberfx/hyperscript/server` renders components to an HTML string with no effects run; `hydrate` / `hydrateRoot` adopt that HTML in the browser. `@fiberfx/render-to-string` 4.0.0 re-exports the same module.

## Read this when

You render a page or an island to HTML on a server or in a test, or you attach components to server-rendered markup in the browser.

## The contract

- `renderToString(vnode, context?): string`. The default export, `render` and `renderToStaticMarkup` are the same function. `context` is the root's initial legacy context object (for `getChildContext`); `createContext` code omits it.
- While rendering to a string, `useEffect` and `useLayoutEffect` callbacks never run, and event handlers are not serialized. `useState` gives its initial value; `useContext` reads providers in the tree.
- `useId`: ids are in tree order (`P0-0`, `P0-1`, …), reset per `renderToString` root, and match after hydration.
- A component that throws a promise makes `renderToString` throw `Error('Use "renderToStringAsync" for suspenseful rendering.')`.
- `renderToStringAsync(vnode, context?)`: always `await` it. It re-renders a suspended component after its promise settles, wraps that output in `<!--$s-->…<!--/$s-->`, and follows at most 25 nested levels. Preview: no test covers it.
- Browser: `hydrate(vnode, parent)` from `@fiberfx/hyperscript`, or `hydrateRoot(container, children)` from `@fiberfx/hyperscript/client`, which returns `{ render, unmount }`. Hydrate the same tree with the same props; the server's nodes are kept.
- `useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot, getServerSnapshot)`: `getServerSnapshot` is read on the server and during hydration; after hydration it re-renders with `getSnapshot`. It subscribes in an effect.

## Minimal example

```tsx
// server
import { renderToString } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript/server";
const html = renderToString(<Counter />); // "<button>0</button>"

// browser
import { hydrateRoot } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript/client";
const app = document.getElementById("app");
if (app) hydrateRoot(app, <Counter />);
```

## Never emit

- `window`, `document` or `navigator` read during render in a component that renders on the server: read them in `useEffect`, or through `useSyncExternalStore` with a `getServerSnapshot`.
- `renderToStringAsync` without `await`.
- `./jsx`, `./stream` or `./stream-node` subpaths of `@fiberfx/render-to-string`: they are not exported.

- Testing and inspecting: /hyperscript/testing/llms.txt
- This companion: /hyperscript/server/llms.txt (the page as Markdown, `/hyperscript/server.md`, is planned for W3)

# Testing and inspecting — Mercury LMS

> HS5 of Mercury Hyperscript. `@fiberfx/hyperscript/test-utils` flushes batched renders and after-paint effects for tests; `./inspect` gives detached records of what the renderer does; `./debug` turns on development checks when imported.

## Read this when

You write a test for a Mercury component, build a tool that watches renders, or need a clear error for a hook, key or `render` mistake.

## The contract

- `act(callback: () => void | Promise<void>): Promise<void>`: runs the callback, then flushes renders and effects until settled. A sync callback is flushed before `act` returns, so no `await` is needed; for an async one, `await act(async () => …)`. Nested calls flush once, at the outermost.
- `setupRerender(): () => void`: queued renders wait until you call the returned function. `teardown()` drains the rest and restores the queue; call it after each such test.
- `onCommit(listener: (root) => void): () => void`: called after each commit, once per root, with the DOM updated.
- `onDiff(listener: () => void): () => void`: test-only, called inside the renderer after each diffed node; a throw stops the render and propagates out of `render`.
- `inspect({ root?, phases?, fn }): Subscription`: `phases` ⊆ `root | render | diffed | commit | unmount | error` (an unknown one throws `TypeError`); `root` is a container passed to `render`/`hydrate`. The record is `{ kind, id, parentId, rootId, type, name, error? }`: detached, `structuredClone`-safe, ids stable across re-renders. It returns `dispose()` (also `.unsubscribe()`). `inspectFailures(): number` counts contained subscriber throws. Importing installs nothing.
- `import "@fiberfx/hyperscript/debug"` (side effect, development only): it throws on an undefined `render` parent, an undefined component, or a hook outside render, and `console.error`s duplicate keys and improper table/paragraph nesting. It exports `getDisplayName`, `getCurrentVNode`, `getOwnerStack`, `captureOwnerStack`, `setupComponentStack` and `resetPropWarnings`.
- Mercury UI's harness, `fiberfx/ui/test/testing.ts`, wraps `render`, `rerender`, `unmount`, `cleanup` and `fireEvent` in `act`; its queries come from `@fiberfx/testing`.

## Minimal example

```tsx
import { expect, it } from "vitest";
import { render } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript";
import { useEffect, useState } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript/hooks";
import { act } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript/test-utils";

function Greeting() {
  const [name, setName] = useState("…");
  useEffect(() => setName("Mercury"), []);
  return <p>Hello, {name}</p>;
}

it("flushes the effect's update", () => {
  const container = document.createElement("div");
  act(() => render(<Greeting />, container));
  expect(container.textContent).toBe("Hello, Mercury");
});
```

## Never emit

- Assertions on the DOM right after a state update outside `act` or `setupRerender`: the render is still queued.
- `options` from the root entry to hook into the renderer: use `./inspect`, or `onCommit`/`onDiff` in tests.
- `onDiff` in application code: it is test-only.
- A testing library for another framework: use `act` from `./test-utils` (Mercury UI's harness builds on it).

# A tested component — Mercury LMS

> HS6, the Mercury Hyperscript capstone. `KindFilter` (`node/apps/echd-os/src/kan/common.tsx`), the kind chips of the KAN squads and messages views, given a written contract and a test: `createRoot` inside `act`, a native click, DOM assertions, `./inspect` commit records, and a server-versus-client markup check. Results are marked: read from an existing test, or not run.

## Read this when

You test a Mercury component end to end, or you change `KindFilter` or another KAN view piece in `common.tsx`.

## The contract (KindFilter)

- Props: `kinds: readonly SquadKindCount[] | null | undefined` (`{ kind: string; count: number | null }`), `picked: readonly string[]`, `onToggle(kind)`, `onClear()`. It is controlled: no state of its own.
- No kinds → renders `null`.
- `div.kan-kinds[role=group][aria-label="Filter by kind"]` → one `button.kan-kind[data-kind=<kind>][aria-pressed=<picked.includes(kind)>]` per kind, keyed by the kind, holding a `Chip` (size `sm`, variant `kindTone(kind)`, `selected` while picked) with the kind and its count (`null` → `0`).
- A click calls `onToggle(kind)`. The ghost `Button` "All kinds" renders only while `picked` is non-empty and calls `onClear()`.
- Used by `SquadsExplorer` (`squads.tsx:91`) and the messages view (`messages.tsx:430`), each with `picked` from its island store.

## The test recipe

- Own `picked` in a harness with `useState`, and mount with `createRoot(el)` and `act(() => root.render(...))`. Unmount with `act(() => root.unmount())`.
- Drive with `act(() => button.click())`: a native click, settled when `act` returns.
- Verified through `SquadsExplorer` (`squads.test.tsx:112-135`): one `.kan-kind` per kind, the text "ask 1", `aria-pressed` "true" after a click, and an "All kinds" button by its text.
- Not run: the group label, `fyi 0`, `is-selected` on the chip, clearing, `null` for no kinds, the commit count per click, no button unmount, and `renderToString(<KindFilter …/>) === el.innerHTML`.
- `inspect({ root: el, phases: ["commit", "unmount"], fn })` → frozen, plain records; `stop()` disposes.
- Live Mercury islands don't hydrate: a `data-ssr` render is replaced on the first paint (`fiberfx/live-mercury/src/hooks.ts:68-71`). Compare the markup, not a hydration.

## Minimal example

```tsx
import { createRoot } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript/client";
import { act } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript/test-utils";
import { KindFilter } from "./common";

const el = document.createElement("div");
const root = createRoot(el);
let toggled = "";
act(() => root.render(<KindFilter kinds={[{ kind: "ask", count: 1 }]} picked={[]} onToggle={(k) => (toggled = k)} onClear={() => {}} />));
act(() => el.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>(".kan-kind[data-kind='ask']")?.click());
// toggled === "ask" (from the source; not run)
act(() => root.unmount());
```

## Never emit

- Pressed state held inside `KindFilter`: `picked` is the owner's.
- DOM assertions outside `act` after a click.
- A claimed result for a check no test has run: mark it "not run".

# Mercury UI, the design system — Mercury LMS

> `@fiberfx/ui` 4.0.0: Mercury's design system. 139 components in ten families, written on `@fiberfx/hyperscript`, styled through enum props and one token sheet. Each component has a hand-written contract, `<Name>.prompt.md`, beside its source. No React.

## Read this when

You build a screen in a Mercury app and need to know which component exists, where it comes from, and how it is styled. This is the course's landing; the chapters follow.

## The contract (tier: Shipped — @fiberfx/ui 4.0.0 on npm since 2026-11-05)

- Components: `import { Button, Card } from "@fiberfx/ui"`. For published 4.0.0, load CSS explicitly: `import "@fiberfx/ui/styles.css"` in native apps, or link the pinned stylesheet in [browser HTML](/start/browser/llms.txt). A component import alone does not establish that styling is loaded.
- CSS alone: `@fiberfx/ui/styles.css` (everything) or `@fiberfx/ui/tokens.css` (tokens only).
- Peers: `@fiberfx/hyperscript` 4.0.0 and `@fiberfx/core` 4.0.0. JSX compiles against `@fiberfx/hyperscript`.
- Families: actions (3), foundations (19), inputs (32), forms (8), selection (15), feedback (8), data-display (17), navigation (11), overlay (11), layout (15).
- Style a component through its enum props (`variant`, `size`, `tone`); style your own layout with `rgb(var(--token))`.
- The `.mx-*` classes (`mx-btn`, `mx-card`, ...) are private: never write them. A component merges your own classes from its `class` prop.
- Also re-exported from `@fiberfx/core`: `cx`, `createFormatter`, `createTimeFormatter`, `useFocusManager`, `useLocale`, `useLocaleFormatters`, `useMessageFormatter`, `createLocaleFormatters`, `createMessageFormatter`, `localeDirection`.

## Minimal example

```tsx
import { Button, Card } from "@fiberfx/ui";

export function SaveCard() {
  return (
    <Card variant="raised" title="Draft">
      <Button variant="primary">Save</Button>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

`Button`: `variant` primary | secondary | outline | ghost | destructive | inverse; `size` sm | md | lg; `loading`, `fullWidth`, `leading`, `trailing`, `type`. `Card`: `variant` flat | raised | floating; `padding`, `title`, `actions`.

## Never emit

An authored `.mx-*` class, a literal colour where a token exists, `npm i`, and any import from `react`, `react-dom` or `effector`.

## Next

# UI0, tokens and themes — Mercury LMS

> Mercury UI's one token sheet, `fiberfx/ui/src/styles/tokens.css` (also `@fiberfx/ui/tokens.css`), holds every colour, type, radius, spacing and shadow value. The theme is the class `.light-theme` or `.dark-theme` on `<html>`; light is the default on `:root`.

## Read this when

You style your own layout in a Mercury app, pick a colour for a state, or switch or set the theme.

## The contract (tier: Shipped — @fiberfx/ui 4.0.0 on npm since 2026-11-05)

- Colour tokens are RGB triplets: always `rgb(var(--token))`. Scrims carry alpha already (`--bg-hover: 28 32 36 / 0.06`), still `rgb(var(--bg-hover))`.
- Everything else is a complete value: `var(--space-16)`, `var(--radius-8)`, `var(--shadow-200)`, `var(--font-primary)`, `var(--text-body-300-size)`.
- Read semantic tokens, not scales: `--bg-*`, `--fg-*`, `--border-*`, `--ring-focus`, `--ring-negative`. Naming: `<role>-<intent>-<variant>-<state>`.
- Surfaces: `--bg-primary` page, `--bg-secondary` raised, `--bg-tertiary` sunken, `--bg-elevated` popover/modal. Text: `--fg-primary`, `--fg-secondary`, `--fg-tertiary`. Hairline: `--border-primary`. Text on a solid: `--fg-on-<intent>`.
- Scales: `--slate-1..12`, `--iris-1..12` (brand), `--indigo-1..12` (active, info, link); `--green-`, `--red-`, `--orange-`, `--plum-` at 3, 9, 11.
- Spacing `--space-2..128`; radii `--radius-2..32`, `--radius-full`; type `--text-body-100..500`, `--text-heading-100..500` (`-size`, `-lh`); weights `--fw-regular|medium|semi-bold|bold|black`; shadows `--shadow-100..600`.
- Focus ring: `box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgb(var(--ring-focus))`.
- Theme: toggle `dark-theme` / `light-theme` on `document.documentElement`, before first paint. A `.dark-theme` wrapper deeper in the page also works: it re-declares the semantic tokens.

## Minimal example

```css
.panel {
  background: rgb(var(--bg-secondary));
  border: 1px solid rgb(var(--border-primary));
  border-radius: var(--radius-8);
  padding: var(--space-16);
}
```

```ts
document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark-theme", dark);
document.documentElement.classList.toggle("light-theme", !dark);
```

## Never emit

A literal colour, size, space or radius where a token exists; `var(--bg-brand)` without `rgb()`; `rgb(var(--shadow-200))`; `<html data-theme>` as a substitute for Mercury UI theme classes (the documentation shell has a separate data-theme contract); an authored `.mx-*` class.

## Limits

In the light theme, `--fg-on-brand` text on `--green-9`, `--orange-9` and `--red-9`, and a glyph on `--orange-9`, are known to fail WCAG AA (`fiberfx/ui/scripts/check-contrast.mjs` LIGHT_DEFECTS). The documentation shell already uses an HttpOnly `theme` cookie, a POST/303 form and server-rendered `data-theme`; with no cookie, CSS follows the system preference. Its switch needs no script. Mercury UI applications use the theme classes described above.

# UI1, where a subtree lives — Mercury LMS

> Mercury UI's environment: one inherited context (from `@fiberfx/core`) that every component reads for its portal host, owner document and window, direction, locale, reduced motion, focus fallback and id prefix. `EnvironmentProvider`, `DirectionProvider` and `LocaleProvider` set it and render no DOM; `Portal` reads the host.

## Read this when

Mercury renders inside an iframe, an embedded editor or an island on someone else's page; a section runs right to left; you localize labels, numbers, dates or plurals.

## The contract (tier: Shipped — @fiberfx/ui 4.0.0 on npm since 2026-11-05)

- `EnvironmentProvider` props: `portalContainer`, `ownerDocument`, `ownerWindow` (each nullable), `direction` (`"ltr" | "rtl"`), `locale` (BCP 47), `reducedMotion` (`"user" | "always" | "never"`, default `"user"`), `focusFallback`, `idPrefix`, `children`.
- Merge rule: an omitted prop inherits from the enclosing provider; `null` means unavailable and is never defaulted. No provider: global `document`, its `body`, `ltr`.
- A disposed or `null` host: overlays render nothing; focus moves to `focusFallback`. On a server every resource is `null`, so portals render nothing.
- Several islands on one page: give each root its own `idPrefix`.
- `Portal({ children, container? })`: `container` wins, else the environment's `portalContainer`; no host renders `null`. Context follows the component tree; DOM events bubble through the host.
- `DirectionProvider({ dir })`, `dir` required; `useDirection()` → `"ltr" | "rtl"`.
- `LocaleProvider({ locale, direction?, catalogs?, fallbackLocales? })`: `locale` required; `direction: "auto"` derives from the script; omitted `catalogs` and `fallbackLocales` inherit.
- `useLocale()` → `{ locale, direction, explicit }`.
- `useLocaleFormatters({ timeZone, numberOptions, dateOptions, listOptions, collationOptions })` → `formatNumber`, `formatDate`, `formatList`, `plural`, `pluralCategory`, `compare`, `contains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`.
- `useMessageFormatter()` → `format(key, values)`, `resolve(key, values)` (with `source`: `catalog | fallback | bundled | missing`), `missing()`. Chain: locale, its parents, each fallback and its parents, then Mercury's bundled English for `mercury.close`, `mercury.clear`, `mercury.loading`, `mercury.moreActions`, `mercury.selectedCount`. An unknown key renders as the key.
- Also exported: `createLocaleFormatters`, `createMessageFormatter`, `localeDirection`, type `MessageCatalogs`.

## Minimal example

```tsx
import { LocaleProvider, useLocaleFormatters, useMessageFormatter } from "@fiberfx/ui";
import type { MessageCatalogs } from "@fiberfx/ui";

const catalogs: MessageCatalogs<"cart.items"> = {
  en: { "cart.items": (v, f) => f.plural(Number(v.count), { one: "# item", other: "# items" }) },
};

function CartLine({ count, total }: { count: number; total: number }) {
  const f = useLocaleFormatters({ numberOptions: { style: "currency", currency: "EUR" } });
  const t = useMessageFormatter();
  return <p>{t.format("cart.items", { count })}, {f.formatNumber(total)}</p>;
}

export const Cart = () => (
  <LocaleProvider locale="en-GB" catalogs={catalogs}>
    <CartLine count={3} total={42.5} />
  </LocaleProvider>
);
```

## Never emit

A second locale store or direction context; a provider expected to set `lang` or `dir` (the application sets both on its own root element); `UiEnvironmentContext.Provider` by hand (render `EnvironmentProvider`, which merges); `ReactNode`, `createPortal` from `react-dom`, or any `react` or `effector` import.

# UI2, actions and layout — Mercury LMS

> Mercury UI's actions, `Button`, `IconButton` and `Link`, and the layout composition tier, `Box`, `Stack`, `Flex`, `Grid`, `Container`, `Spacer`, `GridItem`, `Center`, `Sidebar`, `Cluster`, `Section`, whose spacing and radius props name token-scale steps.

## Read this when

You place a press, an icon-only control or an inline link, or lay out a screen without writing CSS for spacing.

## The contract (tier: Shipped — @fiberfx/ui 4.0.0 on npm since 2026-11-05)

- `Button`: `variant` primary (default) | secondary | outline | ghost | destructive | inverse; `size` sm | md (default) | lg; `loading` (disables, `aria-busy`, spinner replaces the leading icon); `fullWidth`; `leading`; `trailing`; `type` defaults to `"button"`.
- `IconButton`: `icon` and `label` required (`label` → `aria-label` and `title`); `variant` primary | secondary (default) | outline | ghost | destructive; `size` sm | md | lg; `shape` circle (default) | square.
- `Icon` glyphs (38): arrow, arrow-up-right, arrow-down-left, check, close, plus, minus, search, star, bell, cog, user, users, home, list, mail, wallet, credit-card, shield, globe, help-circle, chevron-right, chevron-down, alert, info, download, upload, trash, refresh, copy, pause, play, repeat, trending-up, bank, bolt, flow, batch. `IconName` accepts any string: an unknown name draws nothing.
- `Link`: `<a>` when `href` is set and not `disabled`, else `<button>`; `size` sm | md; `muted`; `leading`; `trailing`; `onClick`; `target`; `rel`.
- Scales (exported types): `SpaceScale` "2".."128" → `var(--space-*)`; `RadiusScale` "2".."32" | "full"; `Align` start | center | end | stretch | baseline; `Justify` start | center | end | between | around | evenly.
- `Box`: `p`/`px`/`py`/`pt`/`pr`/`pb`/`pl`, `bg` primary | secondary | tertiary | brand | brand-subtle | elevated, `radius`, `border`, `shadow` "100".."600".
- `Stack`: `gap`, `align`, `justify`. `Flex`: `direction`, `gap`, `align`, `justify`, `wrap`. `Grid`: `cols`, `rows` (a number = equal tracks, a string = template), `gap`, `flow`, `align`, `justify`.
- Every tier component takes `as` and passes other attributes through.

## Minimal example

```tsx
import { Box, Button, Flex, IconButton } from "@fiberfx/ui";

export const Bar = () => (
  <Box p="16" bg="secondary" radius="8" border>
    <Flex gap="8" align="center" justify="between">
      <IconButton icon="trash" label="Discard" variant="ghost" />
      <Button variant="primary">Save</Button>
    </Flex>
  </Box>
);
```

## Never emit

Scale props as numbers or pixels (`gap={12}`, `gap="12px"`: use `gap="12"`); an `IconButton` without `label`; an icon name outside the set; `<Link disabled href>` expecting an anchor; inline `style` spacing where a scale prop exists; any `react` or `effector` import.

# UI3, inputs and forms — Mercury LMS

> Mercury UI's form composition (`Form`, `Field`, `Label`, `Description`, `FieldError`, `Fieldset`, `Legend`, `FormSection`, `ErrorSummary`) and its inputs (`Input`, `Textarea`, `DateField`, `ColorField` and the rest). A Field hands its control one explicit binding; a Form lets an ErrorSummary find its Fields.

## Read this when

You build a form: label, help text and error around a control, a group of controls, a summary of problems after a failed submit, or a date or color entry.

## The contract (tier: Shipped — @fiberfx/ui 4.0.0 on npm since 2026-11-05)

- `Field` props: `id`, `name`, `label`, `hint`, `error`, `required`, `invalid` (default: `error` present), `disabled`, `readOnly`, `focusTarget`, `class`, `style`, `children` (elements, or `(field) => ...`).
- The binding (`FieldContextValue`): `id`, `name`, `labelId`, `descriptionId`, `errorId` (`<id>-label|-description|-error`), `invalid`, `required`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `focus()`, `getControlProps(own?)`.
- `getControlProps({ "aria-describedby"?, "aria-labelledby"? })` → `id` plus, only when set, `name`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby` (yours first, then hint, then error), `aria-invalid: true`, `required`, `disabled`, `readOnly`. No event handlers. Spread it on the control.
- `useFieldContext()` → the binding, or `null`. Read by `SearchField`, `TokenField`, `CheckboxGroup`, `Combobox`, `CustomSelect`, `ListBox`.
- One label: on the Field or on the control, never both.
- `Description`, `FieldError`: not live regions; give an `id` when used alone.
- `Input`: `label`, `hint`, `error`, `leading`, `trailing`, plus input attributes. `Textarea`: `label`, `hint`, `error`, `resizable`, `size`.
- `Fieldset`: `legend`, `hint`, `error`, `invalid`, `focusTarget`; a native fieldset. `FormSection`: `title`, `open`/`onOpenChange` or `defaultOpen`; closed content is inert; opened before a focus lands inside.
- `Form`: a native form, everything forwarded; `noValidate` is yours to pass; Fields register under `name` and `id`.
- `ErrorSummary`: `title` (required), `issues: { field, message, target? }[]`, `focusRequest` (failed-submit counter; each new positive value focuses once), `headingLevel` (2). Empty issues render nothing.
- `DateField`: `value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange(date | undefined)`, `onValidityChange` (`empty | incomplete | impossible | unavailable | before-min | after-max | valid`), `minValue`, `maxValue`, `isDateUnavailable`, `name` (submits an ISO date), `readOnly`, `locale` ("en"), `label`. Values: `parseDate("2026-11-30")` or `new CalendarDate(y, m, d)` from `@fiberfx/core`.
- `ColorField`: parses on Enter or blur; accepts `#hex`, `rgb()`, `hsl()`, `hsb()`, `color(display-p3 …)`; `editorStates` (`inherit`, `unset`); `tokens` (`{token-id}`); `onChange(value, { reason: commit | token | detach | reset | text })`.

## Minimal example

```tsx
import { useState } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript/hooks";
import { Field, Input } from "@fiberfx/ui";

export function TitleField({ error }: { error?: string }) {
  const [title, setTitle] = useState("");
  return (
    <Field name="title" label="Title" hint="Shown in lists" error={error} required>
      {(field) => <Input {...field.getControlProps()} value={title} onInput={(event) => setTitle(event.currentTarget.value)} />}
    </Field>
  );
}
```

## Never emit

A `label` on both the Field and its Input; cloning children to inject ids; an `aria-live` on a FieldError; a `focusRequest` bumped on every keystroke; a `Date` object as a DateField value; a form-state library inside `Form`; any `react` or `effector` import.
