# UI4, selection — Mercury LMS

> Mercury UI's selection controls: `Checkbox`, `Switch`, `Radio` (native inputs, with Root/Control/Indicator parts), `CheckboxGroup`, `RadioGroup`, the `ListBox` collection with its item and section parts, and `Combobox`, a text input over a suggestion ListBox in virtual focus.

## Read this when

You let a reader choose: a flag, one of a few, several of a few, one or several of many, or one typed and suggested.

## The contract (tier: Shipped — @fiberfx/ui 4.0.0 on npm since 2026-11-05)

- Shared state rule: controlled (`checked`, `value`, `selectedKeys`) is authoritative; a default seeds uncontrolled state and is what a form reset restores.
- `Checkbox`: `checked`, `defaultChecked` (`"mixed"` allowed), `onChange(checked)`, `indeterminate`, `label`, `name`, `value`, `disabled`, `required`, `readOnly`, `invalid`, `id`, `form`. Mixed submits as unchecked.
- `Switch`: same state props; a native checkbox with `role="switch"`.
- `Radio`: `value` (required), `checked`, `onChange(value)`, `label`, `name`, `disabled`, `required`, `invalid`, `id`, `form`.
- Parts: `CheckboxRoot` › `CheckboxControl` + `CheckboxIndicator`; `SwitchRoot` › `SwitchControl` + `SwitchIndicator`; `RadioGroupRoot` › `RadioGroupItem` › `RadioGroupControl` + `RadioGroupIndicator`. Indicators are decorative; parts carry `data-state` (`checked | unchecked`).
- `RadioGroup`: `items: { value, label?, disabled? }[]`, `value`/`defaultValue`, `onChange(value)`, `orientation`, `accent`, `name`, `required`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `invalid`, `form`, `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`.
- `CheckboxGroup`: same `items`, `value`/`defaultValue: string[]`, `onChange(keys)`; inside a Field, named by its label.
- `ListBox`: `selectionMode` (`single` default | `multiple` | `none`), `selectionBehavior` (`toggle` | `replace`), `selectedKeys` (`null` = controlled empty), `defaultSelectedKeys`, `onSelectionChange(keys)`, `disabledKeys`, `disallowEmptySelection`, `focusMode` (`dom` | `virtual`), `focusedKey`, `onFocusedKeyChange`, `shouldFocusWrap`, `autoFocus`, `escapeKeyBehavior`, `disallowTypeAhead`, `name` (hidden input per selected key), `renderEmptyState`. Keys are `CollectionKey` (`string | number`).
- ListBox parts: `ListBoxItem` (`id` required, `textValue`, `disabled`, children or `(state) => ...`), `ListBoxItemText`, `ListBoxItemDescription`, `ListBoxSelectionIndicator`, `ListBoxSection`, `ListBoxLabel`, `ListBoxSeparator`. `getListBoxOptionId(listBoxId, key)`.
- `Combobox` › `ComboboxInput` + `ComboboxContent` › `ListBoxItem`s. `selectedKey`/`defaultSelectedKey`, `onSelectionChange` (on commit only: Enter or a press), `inputValue`/`defaultInputValue`/`onInputChange`, `open`/`onOpenChange(open, details)`, `menuTrigger` (`input` | `focus` | `manual`), `actionKeys` + `onAction`, `clearInputOnCommit`, `allowsEmptyCollection`, `getKeyLabel`, `name`.
- Combobox never commits on Tab or blur (restores the committed text) and does not filter: render the suggestions you want.
- In a Field, ListBox, CheckboxGroup and Combobox take the Field's states and references; the Combobox input takes the Field's id and label.

## Minimal example

```tsx
import { useState } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript/hooks";
import { Combobox, ComboboxContent, ComboboxInput, Field, ListBoxItem, useLocaleFormatters } from "@fiberfx/ui";
import type { CollectionKey } from "@fiberfx/ui";

const authors = [{ id: "ada", label: "Ada Lovelace" }, { id: "grace", label: "Grace Hopper" }];

export function AuthorPicker() {
  const [author, setAuthor] = useState<CollectionKey | null>(null);
  const [text, setText] = useState("");
  const { contains } = useLocaleFormatters();
  return (
    <Field name="author" label="Author">
      <Combobox selectedKey={author} onSelectionChange={setAuthor} onInputChange={setText}>
        <ComboboxInput />
        <ComboboxContent>
          {authors.filter((a) => contains(a.label, text)).map((a) => <ListBoxItem key={a.id} id={a.id}>{a.label}</ListBoxItem>)}
        </ComboboxContent>
      </Combobox>
    </Field>
  );
}
```

## Never emit

A `ListBoxItem` without `id`; a selection committed from `onInputChange` or `onFocusedKeyChange`; an `aria-label` on `ComboboxInput` inside a labelled Field; focus moved into the Combobox popup; an indicator part rendered before its control; a `RangeSlider` (it is `Slider` with a two-number value); any `react` or `effector` import.

# UI5, feedback and data display — Mercury LMS

> Mercury UI's feedback (`Alert`, `Toast` and its parts, `Progress`) and data display (`Card`, `Table`, `DataGrid`), with the rest of both families. All presentational: the application owns timers, sorting, selection state and removal.

## Read this when

You tell a reader something happened, show progress, or show records in a card, a table or an editable grid.

## The contract (tier: Shipped — @fiberfx/ui 4.0.0 on npm since 2026-11-05)

- `Alert`: `tone` `info` (default) | `success` | `warning` | `danger`; `title` (an h4), children, `actions`, `dismissible` + `onDismiss`. `danger` is `role="alert"`, the rest `role="status"`. It never removes itself.
- `Toast`: `tone`, `priority` (`urgent` | `normal`; default urgent for danger), `onDismiss(reason: "close" | "swipe")`, `closeLabel` ("Dismiss"), `swipeDirection` (`left | right | up | down`), `swipeThreshold` (50). Always renders a close control. Owns no timer.
- Toast parts: `ToastViewport` (`label`, default "Notifications"; you position it), `ToastTitle`, `ToastDescription`, `ToastAction` (`altText` required: the other way to do it).
- `Progress`: `value`, `min` (0), `max` (100), clamped; `indeterminate` states no value; `label` or `aria-labelledby`; `valueText`; `variant` `brand | positive | negative | caution | info`; `size` `sm | md | lg`. Pass the final value: completion is never inferred.
- `Card`: `variant` `flat | raised | floating`, `padding` (20), `title`, `actions`.
- `Table`: `columns: Column<Row>[]` (`key`, `label`, `align`, `render`, `sortable`, `resizable`, `required`, widths), `data`, `getRowKey` (index otherwise), `caption`, `striped`, `emptyState` ("No results"), `loading`; `sort` + `onSortChange` (the table never reorders data); `selectionMode` `none | single | multiple`, `selectedKeys`, `onSelectionChange` (controls disabled without it), `isRowDisabled`, `getRowLabel`; `keyboardNavigation`; `columnOrder`, `hiddenColumns`, `columnWidths`, `onColumnWidthsChange`; `expansion` (`detail` or `treegrid`), `expandedKeys`, `onExpandedChange`.
- `DataGrid`: `columns` (`key`, `label`, `editable`, `getValue`, `render`, `align`), `rows` (the window), `getRowKey` (required), `startIndex`/`getRowIndex`, `total` (`null` = unknown), `onCellCommit({ rowKey, column, value })`, `caption`. Arrows, Home/End (Ctrl: first/last row); Enter or F2 edits; Enter commits; Escape cancels. No built-in virtualizer.

## Minimal example

```tsx
import { useState } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript/hooks";
import { Table } from "@fiberfx/ui";
import type { Column, TableSort } from "@fiberfx/ui";

type File = { id: string; name: string; size: number };
const columns: Column<File>[] = [{ key: "name", label: "File", sortable: true }, { key: "size", label: "Size", align: "right" }];

export function Files({ files }: { files: File[] }) {
  const [sort, setSort] = useState<TableSort | null>(null);
  const rows = sort ? [...files].sort((a, b) => (a.name < b.name ? -1 : 1) * (sort.direction === "ascending" ? 1 : -1)) : files;
  return <Table columns={columns} data={rows} getRowKey={(f) => f.id} caption="Files" sort={sort} onSortChange={setSort} />;
}
```

## Never emit

A Toast with a built-in timeout prop (there is none); a Toast whose only dismissal is a swipe; `ToastAction` without `altText`; `danger` for emphasis; a Table expected to sort or filter `data` itself; a DataGrid without `getRowKey`; `total` guessed instead of `null`; an import from any UI framework other than `@fiberfx/hyperscript`.

# UI6, navigation — Mercury LMS

> Mercury UI's navigation: `Tabs` (facade and `TabsRoot`/`TabsList`/`TabsTrigger`/`TabsPanel`), `Breadcrumbs`, `Tree`, `NavigationTree`, `Menubar` (facade and compound parts) and `Toolbar` with its parts. Tabs, Toolbar, Menubar and Tree use one primary Tab stop and arrows inside, mirrored in RTL. Breadcrumbs and NavigationTree keep native link and button navigation; Mercury does not perform application routing.

## Read this when

You build tabs, a breadcrumb trail, an entity tree, a sidebar of route links, a desktop-style menu strip or an editor toolbar.

## The contract (tier: Shipped — @fiberfx/ui 4.0.0 on npm since 2026-11-05)

- `Tabs`: `tabs: { label, value, disabled?, content?, panelId? }[]`, `value`, `onChange(value)`, `activationMode` (`automatic` default | `manual`), `orientation`, `dir`, `loop` (true), `keepMounted` (false), `variant` (`underline` | `pills`).
- Tabs parts: `TabsRoot` (`value`/`defaultValue`/`onValueChange`, same modes) › `TabsList` (`variant`) › `TabsTrigger` (`value`), plus `TabsPanel` (`value`, `keepMounted`).
- `Breadcrumbs` (`label` "Breadcrumbs", `maxItems` ≥ 3, `separator`, `renderLink`, `truncate`, `overflowLabel`, `overflowPanelLabel`) › `Breadcrumb` (`href`, `current` (default: last), `disabled`, `disabledReason`, `id`). Exactly one `aria-current="page"`.
- `Tree`: `nodes: TreeNodeData[]` (`id`, `label`, `kind` `leaf | branch | lazy`, `children`, `disabled`), `expandedIds` (controlled) + `onExpandedChange`, `loadChildren`, `selectionMode` (`none` default), `selectedIds`, `onSelectionChange`, `selectionFollowsFocus`, `activeId`/`onActiveChange`, `onActivate` (Enter), `renderLabel`, `renderActions`, `dir`. `TreeItemAction` (`label`) for per-node actions.
- `NavigationTree`: `label` (required), `nodes: { id, label, href?, target?, rel?, download?, children? }[]`, `currentId`, `expandedIds`/`defaultExpandedIds` (default: the current route's ancestors), `onExpandedChange`, `onNavigate(href, event)` (host routes and calls `preventDefault`), `renderLabel`, `dir`.
- `Menubar`: `menus: { label, icon?, items: { type?, label, id?, group?, value?, checked?, shortcut?, icon?, onSelect?, disabled? }[] }[]`, `accent`, `dir`. Compound: `MenubarRoot` › `MenubarMenuRoot` › `MenubarTrigger` + `MenubarContent` with `MenubarItem`, `MenubarCheckboxItem`, `MenubarRadioGroup`, `MenubarRadioItem`, `MenubarItemIndicator`, `MenubarGroup`, `MenubarLabel`, `MenubarSeparator`, `MenubarSub`, `MenubarSubTrigger`, `MenubarSubContent`.
- `Toolbar`: `orientation`, `dir`, `loop` (true), `size` (`sm | md`), `variant` (`surface | plain`), `focusableWhenDisabled`. Parts: `ToolbarButton`, `ToolbarLink`, `ToolbarGroup`, `ToolbarSeparator`, `ToolbarToggleGroup` (`type: "single"` with `value: string`, or `"multiple"` with `value: string[]`) › `ToolbarToggleItem` (`value`).

## Minimal example

```tsx
import { Breadcrumb, Breadcrumbs } from "@fiberfx/ui";

export const Trail = () => (
  <Breadcrumbs>
    <Breadcrumb href="/">Mercury</Breadcrumb>
    <Breadcrumb href="/ui">UI</Breadcrumb>
    <Breadcrumb href="/ui/navigation">Navigation</Breadcrumb>
  </Breadcrumbs>
);
```

## Never emit

A Tree used for route links (use NavigationTree); a NavigationTree node expected to select; a router call from Breadcrumbs (it never navigates); two current breadcrumbs; `maxItems` below 3; a Tab stop on every toolbar button; Tree expansion assumed to select; an import from any UI framework other than `@fiberfx/hyperscript`.

# Hypergraph, the state kernel — Mercury LMS

> `@fiberfx/hypergraph` 4.0.0: Mercury's state kernel. A scheduler and graph executor for a model's units (store, event, effect) and their wiring, with fork scopes, effects and one observation surface. No dependencies, no React.

## Read this when

You write or change state in a Mercury app: a store, an event, an effect, their wiring, or a scope for a test or a server render. This page is the course's landing; the API by name follows in the reference.

## The contract (tier: Shipped — @fiberfx/hypergraph 4.0.0 on npm since 2026-11-05)

- Units: `store(init, config?)`, `event()`, `effect(handler)`.
- Wiring: `sample({clock, source, filter, fn, target})`, `combine`, `split`, `attach`, `merge`, `restore`, and `on`, `reset`, `map`, `filter`, `filterMap`, `prepend`.
- Scopes: `fork`, `allSettled`, `scopeBind`, `snapshot`, `apply`, `diff`, `dispose`.
- `watch(unit, fn, {scope})`, `kindOf(x)`, `setCarrier`, `HypergraphError`.
- Subpaths: `@fiberfx/hypergraph`, `@fiberfx/hypergraph/node` (`nodeCarrier`), `@fiberfx/hypergraph/inspect` (`inspect`, `describe`). `/hyperscript` and `/hmr` are planned and not exported.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { event, store } from "@fiberfx/hypergraph";

const increment = event<number>();
export const $count = store(0, { name: "$count" }).on(increment, (count, by) => count + by);
```

## Never emit

`createStore`, `createEvent`, `createEffect`, `createDomain`, `guard`, `forward`, `createApi`, `withFactory`, `is`, and any import from `effector` or `effector-react`. They are not Mercury's names.

## Errors

A refusal is a `HypergraphError` with a `code`: `pure-call`, `derived-call`, `derived-target`, `disposed-scope`, `reset-reason`.

# Units: store, event and effect — Mercury LMS

> The three kinds of unit in a Hypergraph model, from `@fiberfx/hypergraph` 4.0.0: `store(init, config?)`, `event<T>(config?)`, `effect(handler)`. A store holds a value, an event carries a payload, an effect runs a handler and settles.

## Read this when

You declare state, a signal or a side effect in a Mercury model, or you need a unit's methods and members.

## The contract (tier: Shipped — @fiberfx/hypergraph 4.0.0 on npm since 2026-11-05)

- `store<T>(init: T, config?)` → `StoreWritable<T>`. Config: `name`, `sid` (authored identity), `skipVoid`, `updateFilter(next, prev)`, `serialize: 'ignore' | {write, read}`, `schema: {id, version}` (shape becomes `<id>@<version>`).
- `StoreWritable`: `.on(clock | clock[], (state, payload) => next)`, `.reset(...clocks)`; both return the store.
- Every `Store`: `.getState()` (caller's scope, else outside any), `.map(fn, {skipVoid?})` (derived), `.updates` (event), `.watch(fn)` (called with the state now, then each update).
- A reducer returning `undefined` is skipped unless `skipVoid: false` (vector `store.on-void-skips`).
- `event<T = void>({name?})` → callable. `.map`, `.filter(fn | {fn})`, `.filterMap` (drop on `undefined`) make derived events; `.prepend(fn)` makes a callable event; `.watch(fn)`.
- `effect<P, D, F = Error>(handler)` → `(params) => Promise<D>`. Members: `done {params, result}`, `doneData`, `fail {params, error}`, `failData`, `finally {status, params, result | error}`, `pending: Store<boolean>`, `inFlight: Store<number>`. With no handler a call fails until `fork({handlers})` supplies one.
- Declared effects (`{request}`, `{channel, payload?}`, `{timer}`) need `fork({performers})`; performers arrive with H4.
- A derived unit can be neither called nor targeted.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { effect, event, store } from "@fiberfx/hypergraph";

const increment = event<number>();
export const $count = store(0, { name: "$count" }).on(increment, (n, by) => n + by);

export const loadUser = effect(async (id: number) => ({ id, name: "Ada" }));
export const $name = store("").on(loadUser.doneData, (_, user) => user.name);
```

## Never emit

`createStore`, `createEvent`, `createEffect`, `store.setState`, `store.off`, `effect.use`, and any import from `effector` or `effector-react`.

## Next

- Wiring units together: /hypergraph/wiring (/hypergraph/wiring/llms.txt)

# Wiring: units into a graph — Mercury LMS

> How `@fiberfx/hypergraph` connects units: `sample` (the one composition primitive), `combine` (stores through a barrier), `split`, `attach`, `merge`, `restore`, and `on`, `reset`, `map`, `filter`, `filterMap`, `prepend` as functions. One launch runs to quiescence, glitch-free.

## Read this when

You connect units: derive a value, route a payload, gate an update on a store, or call an effect with params built from state.

## The contract (tier: Shipped — @fiberfx/hypergraph 4.0.0 on npm since 2026-11-05)

- `sample({clock?, source?, filter?, fn?, target?, batch?})`. `filter`: `Store<boolean>` or `(source, clock) => boolean`; `fn: (source, clock) => out`. With `target` it returns the target; without, a new derived unit. A non-unit field in `source` is a constant.
- A derived unit as `target` throws `HypergraphError` `derived-target`.
- `combine([..] | {..}, fn?, {skipVoid?}?)` or `combine(a, b, …, fn?)` → derived `Store`. One launch updates it once (vector `kernel.diamond-one-update-per-launch`).
- `split({source, clock?, match, cases})` → `void`; `match` is `Store<string>`, `(v) => caseName`, or `{case: predicate | Store<boolean>}`. `split(source, {case: predicate})` → `{case: Event, …, __: Event}` (`__` = no match).
- `attach({effect, source?, mapParams?: (params, source) => q})` → new `Effect`; `effect` may be `(source, params) => result`.
- `merge(units[])` → `Event`. `restore(unit, init)` → `StoreWritable` of the last payload; single-unit form only.
- `on(store, clock, fn)`, `reset(store, ...clocks)`, `map(unit, fn)`, `filter(event, fn)`, `filterMap(event, fn)`, `prepend(event, fn)` equal the unit methods.
- Units of two generations cannot be wired together.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { event, sample, store } from "@fiberfx/hypergraph";

const submit = event();
const $text = store("");
export const $sent = store<string[]>([]);

sample({
  clock: submit,
  source: { text: $text, sent: $sent },
  filter: ({ text }) => text.length > 0,
  fn: ({ text, sent }) => [...sent, text],
  target: $sent,
});
```

## Never emit

`guard`, `forward`, `createApi`, `restore({...})` or `restore([...])`, `withFactory`, and any import from `effector`. Use `sample` and `.on` instead.

## Next

- Scopes: /hypergraph/scopes (/hypergraph/scopes/llms.txt)
- This companion: /hypergraph/wiring/llms.txt (the page as Markdown, `/hypergraph/wiring.md`, is planned for W3)

<!-- /hypergraph/scopes/llms.txt -->

# Scopes: fork, settle, hand over — Mercury LMS

> A scope is one isolated copy of a model's state in `@fiberfx/hypergraph`. `fork` makes one, `allSettled` steps it, `scopeBind` binds a function to it, `snapshot`/`diff`/`apply` move its frames by sid with each value's shape, `dispose` ends it.

## Read this when

You write a test, render on a server, hand state from server to client, or run code from a timer or callback inside a scope.

## The contract (tier: Shipped — @fiberfx/hypergraph 4.0.0 on npm since 2026-11-05)

- `Scope` = `{id, gen}`; the handle survives a hot swap and rebinds to the committed generation.
- `fork({values?, handlers?, performers?})`. `values`: `[[store, v], …]`, `{sid: v}`, or a `Snapshot`. `handlers`: `[[effect, fn | effect], …]`, scope-local.
- `allSettled(unit, {scope, params?})` → resolves when nothing is in flight; for an effect `{status: 'done' | 'fail', value}`. `allSettled(scope)` waits for in-flight work.
- `scopeBind(fn, {scope?, safe?})`: binds to `scope` or the caller's; no scope and no `safe` throws. Read a value: `scopeBind(() => $s.getState(), {scope})()`.
- `snapshot(scope, {ignore?})` → `{format: 'mhg-scope/1', gen, values: {sid: {shape, schema?, value}}}`: writable stores with a sid that the scope changed or was given; `serialize: 'ignore'` stays out.
- `diff(scope, since)` → `{format, gen, from, changed, removed}`.
- `apply(scope, snapshot | diff)` → `Miss[]` `{unit: sid, reason: {kind: 'removed'} | {kind: 'shape', from, to}}`; an entry is taken only on the same sid and shape. Misses also go to `inspect` as `reset`.
- Shape until the compiler emits one: `runtime:<structure>` (e.g. `runtime:number`); with `schema` it is `<id>@<version>`.
- `dispose(scope)`: stops work and scoped watches, settles waiting `allSettled`; later `allSettled` or an effect call there rejects `HypergraphError` `disposed-scope`.
- A store needs a `sid` to travel in a frame.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { allSettled, event, fork, scopeBind, snapshot, store } from "@fiberfx/hypergraph";

const increment = event();
const $count = store(0, { sid: "count" }).on(increment, (n) => n + 1);

export async function run() {
  const scope = fork({ values: [[$count, 3]] });
  await allSettled(increment, { scope });
  return { now: scopeBind(() => $count.getState(), { scope })(), frame: snapshot(scope) };
}
```

## Never emit

`serialize`, `hydrate`, `fork(domain)`, `createDomain`, and any import from `effector`. Use `snapshot` and `apply`.

# Observing: watch, inspect, describe — Mercury LMS

> How code and tools see a `@fiberfx/hypergraph` model. `watch(unit, fn, {scope})` for a unit's updates, owned by its generation; `inspect` and `describe` from `@fiberfx/hypergraph/inspect`, the one observation surface.

## Read this when

You react to updates outside the graph, write a test that asserts what happened, or build a log, overlay or DevTools view of a model.

## The contract (tier: Shipped — @fiberfx/hypergraph 4.0.0 on npm since 2026-11-05)

- `watch(unit, fn, {scope?})` → `Subscription` (callable; `.unsubscribe()` is the same). Updates only: a store's current state is NOT delivered at once. With `scope`, only that scope's updates; without, the work outside any scope. Ends when its scope's work stops or its generation is retired, whichever first.
- `$store.watch(fn)` differs: called with the state now, then each update.
- `inspect({scope?, kinds?, fn})` from `@fiberfx/hypergraph/inspect` → `Subscription`. Scoped: that scope only; unscoped: no scoped work. Last unsubscribe stops recording.
- `Observation`: `{type, unit, scope, gen, value, cause}`, where `unit` is a sid or run-time identity; additional fields: `fresh?` (declare), `owner?`, `reason?` (reset), `at?` (perform, settle).
- `Kind`: `update`, `skip` (filter, equal or undefined update, updateFilter refusal), `fail` (user function threw), `declare` (value: `Declaration {unit, kind, sid?, name?, derived?, owner?, gen}`; unscoped inspectors only), `perform`, `settle`, `reset`.
- A `fresh` declare is a new store: information, not a reset.
- `describe(reason)` → `removed` | `shape changed from <from> to <to>` | `renamed (a hint, not applied: it may now be <to>)` | `positional` | `new`.
- Types from `/inspect`: `Observation`, `Declaration`, `Kind`, `ResetReason`.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { allSettled, event, fork, store, watch } from "@fiberfx/hypergraph";
import { inspect } from "@fiberfx/hypergraph/inspect";

const increment = event();
const $count = store(0, { sid: "count" }).on(increment, (n) => n + 1);

export async function run() {
  const scope = fork();
  const stop = watch($count, (n) => console.log("count", n), { scope });
  const sub = inspect({ scope, kinds: ["update", "skip"], fn: (o) => console.log(o.type, o.unit) });
  await allSettled(increment, { scope });
  stop();
  sub.unsubscribe();
}
```

## Never emit

`createWatch`, `inspectGraph`, `inspectObserverFailures`, the `Message` type, and any import from `effector` or `effector/inspect`.

# Kinds, carriers and errors — Mercury LMS

> `kindOf(x)` tells a unit's kind or a scope from anything else; `setCarrier(nodeCarrier())` keeps a scope across an `await` on a JavaScript server; every refusal of `@fiberfx/hypergraph` is a `HypergraphError` with a portable `code`.

## Read this when

You branch on what a value is, run Hypergraph on a server with concurrent requests, or handle, test or explain a Hypergraph error.

## The contract (tier: Shipped — @fiberfx/hypergraph 4.0.0 on npm since 2026-11-05)

- `kindOf(x)` → `'store' | 'event' | 'effect' | 'scope' | null`; `null` for anything not made by this module.
- `setCarrier(carrier | null)`. Default none: an effect called in a scope restores that scope to its caller on settle, so an unrelated call during the await can join it. A carrier (`{current(), run(scope, fn)}`) carries the scope down the chain.
- `nodeCarrier()` from `@fiberfx/hypergraph/node` (AsyncLocalStorage). Call `setCarrier(nodeCarrier())` once at server start. Never import `/node` in browser code.
- `HypergraphError extends Error`: `name` `"HypergraphError"`, `code: ErrorCode`. Match on `code`, never on the message.
- Codes: `derived-call` (derived unit called; thrown), `derived-target` (derived unit as `sample` target or `split` case; thrown at wiring), `pure-call` (unit called inside a reducer, `map`, filter; reported, not thrown), `disposed-scope` (work in a disposed scope; `allSettled` or the effect call rejects), `reset-reason` (bad reset reason at the hot-replacement port; not reachable from app code).
- A throw inside any function the graph runs goes to `console.error`, stops that branch, and is observed as `fail`; it never escapes the launch.
- Plain `Error` (no code): units of two generations wired together; a non-unit where a unit is expected; `scopeBind` with no scope and no `safe`; `allSettled` on a derived unit; a declared effect with no performer.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { HypergraphError, allSettled, dispose, event, fork } from "@fiberfx/hypergraph";

const ping = event();

export async function afterDispose() {
  const scope = fork();
  dispose(scope);
  try {
    await allSettled(ping, { scope });
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof HypergraphError && error.code === "disposed-scope") return "fork a new scope";
    throw error;
  }
}
```

## Never emit

`is`, `is.store`, `is.scope`, a check of an error's message text, a unit call inside `.on`/`.map`/`filter` (use `sample`), and any import from `effector`.

<!-- /hypergraph/hot-replacement/llms.txt -->

# Hot replacement: the swap — Mercury LMS

> How `@fiberfx/hypergraph` carries a model's state across a code edit: a body-only edit swaps function slots in place; any other edit loads a new generation and keeps each store whose sid and shape match, naming a reason for every one it drops. Built inside the package; `@fiberfx/hypergraph/hmr` and `mx dev`'s delivery are planned.

## Read this when

You explain why a value survived or reset after an edit, design a model's stores so they survive edits, or read an `hmr:` log line or a `reset` observation.

## The contract (tier: Planned — built and vector-tested, not exported, not delivered by mx dev; today an edit reloads the page)

- Slots mode: every changed module equals the loaded one except function bodies → bodies swapped in place; scope, values, watchers, in-flight effects unchanged.
- Swap mode, otherwise: new generation; restore only kept sids; commit; report; dispose the old generation. Watches made by the old generation's code end with it. `Scope` handles move to the committed generation.
- Takes part: writable stores with a sid (regions included). Not: events, effects, derived stores, sid-less stores, `serialize: 'ignore'` on either side.
- keep: same sid and shape. A changed `init` within one shape keeps the value.
- new: sid only in the new generation; information, not a reset.
- reset reasons (`ResetReason`): `{kind: 'shape', from, to}`, `{kind: 'removed'}`, `{kind: 'renamed', to}` (hint on the OLD sid, never applied; needs a name shared by exactly one removed and one new store), `{kind: 'positional'}` (positional keys never keep in a changed module).
- Shape today: `runtime:<structure of init>`, object keys sorted, e.g. `runtime:object{age:number,name:string}`. Adding a field resets.
- Lists are sorted in UTF-16 code-unit order of sid.
- Each reset/new → an `inspect` `reset`/`declare fresh` observation and a log line `hmr: <sid>: <describe(reason)>`.
- Refusals: `DiffError` `duplicate-sid` | `no-shape`; the update throws, the loaded generation stays live, the caller reloads. An update during an update is refused.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { store } from "@fiberfx/hypergraph";

// before: store(0, { sid: "count" })  → shape runtime:number
// after:  store({}, { sid: "count" }) → shape runtime:object{}
// result: reset count, "shape changed from runtime:number to runtime:object{}"
export const $count = store({}, { sid: "count" });
export const $user = store(null, { sid: "user" }); // kept
```

## Never emit

An import from `@fiberfx/hypergraph/hmr` (not exported yet), `createRootScope`, `hmrScope`, an "init changed" reason, a rename that moves a value to the new sid, and any import from `effector`.

# Server rendering: a scope per request — Mercury LMS

> Render a `@fiberfx/hypergraph` model on a server: `fork()` per request, `await allSettled(...)`, `snapshot(scope)` → JSON frame keyed by sid, `dispose(scope)`; on the client `apply(fork(), frame)` or `fork({values: frame})`. On a JavaScript server, `setCarrier(nodeCarrier())` once at startup keeps each request's scope across `await`.

## Read this when

You render a Mercury page on a server, hand state to the browser, or debug a value that leaked between concurrent requests.

## The contract (tier: Shipped — @fiberfx/hypergraph 4.0.0 on npm since 2026-11-05)

- Server: `const scope = fork({handlers?})`; `await allSettled(event, {scope, params})` waits for every effect the launch started; `const frame = snapshot(scope)`; `dispose(scope)`; send `JSON.stringify(frame)`.
- Client: `apply(fork(), frame as Snapshot)` → `Miss[]` (`removed` | `shape {from, to}`); or `fork({values: frame})`, which reports misses as `reset` observations only.
- Frame: `{format: 'mhg-scope/1', gen, values: {sid: {shape, schema?, value}}}`. Keys are sids, so it applies across builds.
- Travels: writable stores with a sid that the scope changed or was given. Not: sid-less stores, derived stores (client recomputes), `serialize: 'ignore'` stores, stores still at their init.
- Non-JSON values: `serialize: {write(v), read(raw)}`; `apply` runs `read`.
- Carrier: default none (an effect restores its caller's scope on settle; a stray call during an await can join a suspended scope). `setCarrier(nodeCarrier())` from `@fiberfx/hypergraph/node` carries the scope down each async chain. Package test: leak probe reads global 0 / scope 1 by default, global 1 / scope 0 under the carrier.
- Callbacks from outside the chain: `scopeBind(fn, {scope})`.
- Never import `@fiberfx/hypergraph/node` in browser code.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { allSettled, dispose, fork, snapshot, type Snapshot, apply } from "@fiberfx/hypergraph";
import { pageOpened } from "./model";

export async function render(id: number) {
  const scope = fork();
  await allSettled(pageOpened, { scope, params: id });
  const text = JSON.stringify(snapshot(scope));
  dispose(scope);
  return text;
}

export const resume = (text: string) => apply(fork(), JSON.parse(text) as Snapshot);
```

## Never emit

`serialize(scope)`, `hydrate(...)`, `fork(domain)`, one scope shared across requests, `snapshot` before `allSettled` resolves, and any import from `effector`.

# Testing a model: a scope per test — Mercury LMS

> Test a `@fiberfx/hypergraph` model with one `fork()` per test: replace effect handlers per scope, drive with `allSettled`, read with `scopeBind(() => $s.getState(), {scope})()` or `snapshot(scope)`, assert observations with `inspect`. Tests run under `mx test` (headless browser; `vitest` maps to mx's runtime). The conformance vectors in `specs/mercury/vectors/hypergraph/` are the kernel's behaviour as data.

## Read this when

You write or fix a test for a Mercury model, need to fake an effect, or want to know exactly what the kernel does in a case (find its vector).

## The contract (tier: Shipped — @fiberfx/hypergraph 4.0.0 on npm since 2026-11-05)

- One `fork()` per test. A new scope reads every store's init, even after unscoped calls; a scoped launch never touches the global state.
- `fork({values: [[store, v]], handlers: [[effect, fn | effect]]})`: scope-local values and handlers; no module mocking.
- `await allSettled(event, {scope, params})`; for an effect it resolves `{status: 'done', value}` or `{status: 'fail', value: error}` (never rejects for a handler failure).
- Read: `scopeBind(() => $s.getState(), {scope})()`; `snapshot(scope).values[sid]` → `{shape, value}`; empty `{}` before any change.
- `inspect({scope, kinds, fn})` before driving, unsubscribe after. Every update reported once, in launch order. Assert no `fail`: a throwing reducer never throws out of the launch, it only logs and observes `fail`.
- `watch($s, fn, {scope})` reports updates only (no initial call).
- `mx test`: files `*.test.*` / `*.spec.*` (js, mjs, jsx, ts, mts, tsx); `import {describe, test, expect} from "vitest"`; exit 0 pass, 1 fail or none ran, 3 no browser. Do not use `@fiberfx/hypergraph/node` in these tests.
- Vectors: `{format: 'hgv/1', family, vectors}`; id `<family>.<name>`; keys `units`, `wiring`, `steps`, `expect` (`trace` = total order within a launch, `state`, `scopes`, `spies`, `errors` by `{code}`, `inspected`); functions in hgx/1 (`{arg: n}`, `{op, args}`, `{lit}`); `{"$undef": true}`, `{"$error": msg}`. `protocol.json` = Hypergraph's own rules (`observed {by, rule, why}`); `hmr.json` = the swap's diff.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { expect, test } from "vitest";
import { allSettled, effect, fork } from "@fiberfx/hypergraph";

const loadUser = effect(async (id: number) => ({ name: `remote ${id}` }));

test("loads a user", async () => {
  const scope = fork({ handlers: [[loadUser, async (id: number) => ({ name: `user ${id}` })]] });
  expect(await allSettled(loadUser, { scope, params: 7 })).toEqual({ status: "done", value: { name: "user 7" } });
});
```

## Never emit

Tests that call units outside a scope and read global state, module mocks for effects (use `handlers`), `effect.use`, `serialize`, `npm test`/`node --test`/Vite runners for app tests (use `mx test`), and any import from `effector`.

# Models at scale: structure and identity — Mercury LMS

> How to lay out an app-sized `@fiberfx/hypergraph` model: one module per feature, callable events in and derived stores out, a unique feature-prefixed `sid` on every store that travels, every outside call in an effect, wiring across features in one graph. No app in the repository imports `@fiberfx/hypergraph` yet; the worked consumers (echd-os, edu-island-kan, analytics) follow their migration slices.

## Read this when

You split a model into feature modules, choose sids, decide which stores travel in a frame, or expose a feature's state to other features.

## The contract (tier: Shipped — @fiberfx/hypergraph 4.0.0 on npm since 2026-11-05)

- Units belong to the generation of the code that made it; all modules of an app load into one generation; units of two generations cannot be wired together.
- Types draw the surface: `EventCallable<T>` callable, derived `Event<T>` not; `StoreWritable<T>` has `.on`/`.reset`, `Store<T>` not. Exporting a writable store as `Store<T>` is a compile-time fence only.
- Run time: calling a derived unit → `HypergraphError` `derived-call`; derived `target` → `derived-target`.
- Sids: unique per generation. Module loading through the port refuses a sid claimed twice (in one module or across modules), naming both; the swap's diff refuses `duplicate-sid`. Plain `store()` calls are not checked; a frame looks a repeated sid up as its first store; the second's fate is unstated — never rely on it. Prefix by feature (`cart/items`).
- Effects: outside calls only in effects; `fork({handlers})` replaces them per scope; `attach({effect, source, mapParams})` builds params from state; a handler marks the effect JS-only, a declared spec is data (preview).
- Travels: writable + `sid` + not `serialize: 'ignore'`; non-JSON values need `serialize: {write, read}`; derived stores never travel. The same stores are the ones a hot swap keeps or resets.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { event, store, type Store } from "@fiberfx/hypergraph";

export const itemAdded = event<{ id: string; price: number }>();
const $items = store<{ id: string; price: number }[]>([], { sid: "cart/items" })
  .on(itemAdded, (items, item) => [...items, item]);

export const items: Store<{ id: string; price: number }[]> = $items;
export const total = $items.map((list) => list.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price, 0));
```

## Never emit

A sid shared by two stores, a store meant to travel without a `sid`, a fetch or timer inside `.on`/`.map`/`sample`'s `fn`, `withFactory`, `createDomain`, and any import from `effector` or `@fiberfx/hypergraph/hmr`.

## Next

- The capstone: /hypergraph/capstone (/hypergraph/capstone/llms.txt)
- This companion: /hypergraph/models/llms.txt

# Capstone: a model, round-tripped — Mercury LMS

> One `@fiberfx/hypergraph` model built from the exports, run in a `fork()`, its frame taken with `snapshot`, applied into a fresh scope with `fork({values: frame})`, proven equal with `diff(replica, frame)`, then kept in step with `apply(replica, diff(scope, frame))`. Expected values are read from the package's own test, `fiberfx/hypergraph/test/api-types.test.ts`.

## Read this when

You need a complete, correct pattern for a model plus its test with a snapshot round-trip, e.g. server-to-client handoff or a replica kept current by diffs.

## The contract (tier: Shipped — @fiberfx/hypergraph 4.0.0 on npm since 2026-11-05)

- Only writable stores with a `sid` enter a frame; derived stores recompute on the replica.
- `await allSettled(event, {scope, params})` settles effects started by `sample` too.
- `snapshot(scope)` → `{format: 'mhg-scope/1', gen, values: {sid: {shape, value}}}`.
- `fork({values: frame})` = new scope + apply the frame.
- Equality: `diff(replica, frame)` → `changed: {}` (no entry new or different) and `removed: []` (no frame entry missing). `changed` is asserted by the package's test; `removed` is read from the kernel, not run.
- Step: `apply(replica, diff(scope, since))`.
- A call outside any scope (`add(5)`) changes only the global state, never a scope.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { expect, test } from "vitest";
import { allSettled, apply, diff, event, fork, scopeBind, snapshot, store } from "@fiberfx/hypergraph";

const add = event<number>();
const $count = store(0, { sid: "count" }).on(add, (n, by) => n + by);
const read = (scope: ReturnType<typeof fork>) => scopeBind(() => $count.getState(), { scope })();

test("round-trips its frame", async () => {
  const scope = fork();
  await allSettled(add, { scope, params: 3 });
  const frame = snapshot(scope);              // values.count = { shape: "runtime:number", value: 3 }
  const replica = fork({ values: frame });
  expect(read(replica)).toBe(3);
  expect(diff(replica, frame).changed).toEqual({});
  await allSettled(add, { scope, params: 1 });
  apply(replica, diff(scope, frame));
  expect(read(replica)).toBe(4);
});
```

## Never emit

`serialize`, `hydrate`, a store without a `sid` expected to travel, a comparison of `getState()` outside the scope as proof of the replica, and any import from `effector` or `@fiberfx/hypergraph/hmr`.

- The course: /hypergraph (/hypergraph/llms.txt)
- This companion: /hypergraph/capstone/llms.txt

# Coming from Effector — Mercury LMS

> Where each Effector concept lives in Hypergraph (`@fiberfx/hypergraph` 4.0.0), Mercury's state kernel. Rule: a name changes only when its contract or its IR kind changed. Unit constructors are renamed, composition is kept, the scope speaks frames, and domains, `guard`, `forward`, `createApi`, `is` and `withFactory` are retired.

## Read this when

You are translating Effector code or Effector knowledge into a Mercury model, or a user asks "what is X from Effector in Mercury?". This is the only page on the site that uses Effector's names; never emit them as code.

## The map (Effector → Hypergraph)

| Effector | Hypergraph |
|---|---|
| `createStore(init, cfg)` | `store(init, cfg)`; cfg adds `schema` |
| `createEvent()` | `event({name?})` |
| `createEffect(fn)` | `effect(fn)` or `effect(spec)` |
| `sample` `combine` `split` `attach` `merge` `restore` | same names |
| `.on` `.reset` `.map` `.getState` `.updates` `.watch` (store) | same |
| `.map` `.filter` `.filterMap` `.prepend` `.watch` (event) | same |
| `.done` `.doneData` `.fail` `.failData` `.finally` `.pending` `.inFlight` | same |
| `fork({values, handlers})` | `fork({values, handlers, performers})`; `values` may be a snapshot |
| `allSettled` | same (unit + `{scope, params}`, or a scope alone) |
| `scopeBind(unit, cfg)` | `scopeBind(fn, cfg)` |
| `serialize(scope)` | `snapshot(scope)` → `{format: "mhg-scope/1", gen, values: {[sid]: {shape, value}}}` |
| `hydrate(scope, {values})` | `apply(scope, frame)` → misses |
| — | `diff(scope, since)`, `dispose(scope)` |
| `createWatch({unit, fn, scope})` | `watch(unit, fn, {scope})` |
| `is.store(x)` etc. | `kindOf(x) === "store"` |
| `guard` | `sample({clock, source, filter, target})` |
| `forward({from, to})` | `sample({clock: from, target: to})` |
| `createApi` | one `event` + `.on` per key |
| `inspect`, `inspectGraph` | `inspect({scope?, kinds?, fn})` from `@fiberfx/hypergraph/inspect` |
| `useUnit`, `Provider` | not exported yet (planned at `/hyperscript`) |

## No equivalent

`createDomain` and domain hooks, `fork(domain)`, `hydrate(domain)`, `withFactory`, `withRegion`, `createNode`, `launch`, `step`, `clearNode`, `fromObservable`, `setStoreName`, `store.setState`, `store.off`, `store.reinit`, `effect.use`, `useStoreMap`, `useList`, `useGate`, `createGate`, `createComponent`, `connect`. Rewrite the code; do not invent a shim.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { event, sample, store } from "@fiberfx/hypergraph";

const increment = event<number>();
const saved = event<number>();
export const $count = store(0, { name: "$count" }).on(increment, (n, by) => n + by);
sample({ clock: increment, source: $count, target: saved });
```

## Never emit

Any import from `effector`, `effector-react` or `@fiberfx/effector`; `createStore`, `createEvent`, `createEffect`, `createDomain`, `guard`, `forward`, `createApi`, `withFactory`, `is`, `serialize`, `hydrate`, `createWatch`.

- /hypergraph/coming-from-effector/frameworks/llms.txt

# Units and wiring (coming from Effector) — Mercury LMS

> Effector's units and composition in Hypergraph (`@fiberfx/hypergraph`): `store`/`event`/`effect` replace the `create*` constructors; `sample`, `combine`, `split`, `attach`, `merge`, `restore` and the unit methods retain their names, but restore supports only the single-unit form; `guard`, `forward` and `createApi` are rewritten with `sample` and `.on`.

## Read this when

You are porting an Effector model's units or wiring, or writing one from Effector habits.

## Units

| Effector | Hypergraph |
|---|---|
| `createStore(init, {name, sid, serialize, updateFilter, skipVoid})` | `store(init, {…same, schema?})` |
| `$s.on` `.reset` `.map` `.getState` `.updates` `.watch` | same |
| `$s.setState` `.off` `.reinit` | not in the API: use an event + `.on` / `.reset` |
| `createEvent<T>()` | `event<T>({name?})` |
| `ev.filter({fn})` | `ev.filter(fn)` or `ev.filter({fn})` |
| `createEffect(handler)` | `effect<P, D>(handler)` |
| `fx.use(handler)` | not in the API: `fork({handlers: [[fx, handler]]})` |
| — | `effect({request} \| {channel} \| {timer})`: declared; needs `fork({performers})` until H4 |

Notes: `$s.watch(fn)` fires now and on updates; `watch($s, fn)` fires on updates only. `getState()` reads the caller's scope. `sid` is the compiler's job by design, but today its sid pass covers only the legacy facade: write `sid` on a store that must travel or survive an edit (an unnamed unit gets a run-time `api:<n>`).

## Wiring

`sample({clock, source, filter, fn, target, batch})` — returns `target`, or a new unit without one.
`combine(shape, fn?)` or `combine($a, $b, fn?)` — non-store fields are constants.
`split({source, clock?, match, cases})`, or `split(source, match)` → `{[case]: Event, __: Event}`.
`attach({effect, source?, mapParams?})` — `effect` may be `(source, params) => …`.
`merge([units])`, `restore(unit, init)`. Also as functions: `on`, `reset`, `map`, `filter`, `filterMap`, `prepend`.

## Rewrites

| Effector | Hypergraph |
|---|---|
| `guard({clock, filter, target})` | `sample({clock, filter, target})` |
| `forward({from, to})` | `sample({clock: from, target: to})` |
| `createApi($s, {a: fnA, b: fnB})` | `const a = event(); $s.on(a, fnA)` per key |

## Minimal example

```ts
import { effect, event, sample, store } from "@fiberfx/hypergraph";

const fetchUserFx = effect<number, string>(async (id) => `user ${id}`);
const opened = event<number>();
const $enabled = store(true);
export const $user = store<string | null>(null).on(fetchUserFx.doneData, (_, u) => u);
sample({ clock: opened, filter: $enabled, target: fetchUserFx });
```

## Errors

`HypergraphError.code`: `pure-call` (a pure fn called a unit), `derived-call`, `derived-target`, `disposed-scope`, `reset-reason`.

## Never emit

`createStore`, `createEvent`, `createEffect`, `guard`, `forward`, `createApi`, `.setState`, `.use`, `.off`, `.reinit`, or any import from `effector`.

## Navigation

- [Read this page in the browser](/hypergraph/coming-from-effector/units-and-wiring)
- [Agent index](/llms.txt)
- [All English companions](/llms-full.txt)
- [Sitemap](/sitemap.xml)
- [Course companion](/hypergraph/llms.txt)

# Scopes and testing (coming from Effector) — Mercury LMS

> Effector's scope model in Hypergraph (`@fiberfx/hypergraph`): `fork`, `allSettled`, `scopeBind` keep their names; `serialize` → `snapshot` (a frame), `hydrate` → `apply` (returns misses); `diff` and `dispose` are new; no domains; no `scope.getState`.

## Read this when

You are porting Effector tests, SSR serialization or scope handling, or reading a store's value in a scope.

## The map

| Effector | Hypergraph |
|---|---|
| `fork({values, handlers})` | `fork({values, handlers, performers})` |
| `fork(domain, cfg)` | none: `fork(cfg)` |
| `values: [[$s, v]]` or `{[sid]: v}` | same, or a `snapshot` frame |
| `handlers: [[fx, fn]]` | same (`fn` or another effect) |
| `allSettled(unit, {scope, params})`, `allSettled(scope)` | same |
| `scope.getState($s)` | `scopeBind(() => $s.getState(), {scope})()` |
| `scopeBind(unit, {scope, safe})` | `scopeBind(fn, {scope, safe})` |
| `serialize(scope, {ignore})` | `snapshot(scope, {ignore})` |
| `serialize(...)[sid]` | `snapshot(...).values[sid].value` |
| `serialize(..., {onlyChanges})` | no option |
| `hydrate(scope, {values})` → void | `apply(scope, frame)` → `[{unit, reason: {kind: "removed"} \| {kind: "shape", from, to}}]` |
| — | `diff(scope, since)` → `{format, gen, from, changed, removed}` |
| — | `dispose(scope)`; later calls → `HypergraphError` `disposed-scope` |
| `createWatch({unit, fn, scope})` | `watch(unit, fn, {scope})` |

Frame: `{format: "mhg-scope/1", gen, values: {[sid]: {shape, schema?, value}}}`. Only stores with a sid appear; today a sid is written by hand (the compiler's sid pass covers only the legacy facade).

## Minimal example (a test)

```ts
import { allSettled, effect, fork, scopeBind, store } from "@fiberfx/hypergraph";

const fetchUserFx = effect<number, string>(async (id) => `real ${id}`);
const $user = store<string | null>(null).on(fetchUserFx.doneData, (_, u) => u);

const scope = fork({ handlers: [[fetchUserFx, async (id: number) => `stub ${id}`]] });
await allSettled(fetchUserFx, { scope, params: 7 });
scopeBind(() => $user.getState(), { scope })(); // "stub 7"
```

## The scope across an await

Default (browser): as Effector, a settled effect restores its caller's scope, so an unrelated call during the await can join it; capture with `scopeBind`. Node: `setCarrier(nodeCarrier())`, with `nodeCarrier` from `@fiberfx/hypergraph/node`.

## Never emit

`serialize`, `hydrate`, `fork(domain)`, `scope.getState`, `createWatch`, `fx.use`, or any import from `effector`.

## Navigation

- [Read this page in the browser](/hypergraph/coming-from-effector/scopes-and-testing)

- [All English companions](/llms-full.txt)
- [Sitemap](/sitemap.xml)
- [Course companion](/hypergraph/llms.txt)

# Frameworks, after effector-react — Mercury LMS

> Mercury's only view layer is Mercury Hyperscript (`@fiberfx/hyperscript`, hooks at `@fiberfx/hyperscript/hooks`). The Hypergraph bindings `useUnit` and `Provider` are planned at `@fiberfx/hypergraph/hyperscript` and NOT exported yet. Until then, read a store with `useSyncExternalStore` + `watch` + `getState`, unscoped.

## Read this when

You are porting a component that used effector-react, effector-vue or effector-solid, or you need a store's value in a Hyperscript component.

## The map

| effector-react | Mercury |
|---|---|
| `useUnit`, `Provider` | planned at `@fiberfx/hypergraph/hyperscript`; not importable today |
| `useStore` | none (deprecated for `useUnit`) |
| `useEvent` | none |
| `useStoreMap` | none: derive with `.map` / `combine`, then read |
| `useList` | none: map the array in JSX |
| `useGate`, `createGate`, `connect`, `createComponent` | none |
| effector-vue, effector-solid | none |

Hyperscript hooks: `useState`, `useReducer`, `useRef`, `useEffect`, `useLayoutEffect`, `useCallback`, `useMemo`, `useContext`, `useImperativeHandle`, `useDebugValue`, `useErrorBoundary`, `useId`, `useSyncExternalStore`.

## Minimal example (today, outside any scope)

```tsx
import { useSyncExternalStore } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript/hooks";
import { event, store, watch, type Store } from "@fiberfx/hypergraph";

const increment = event<number>();
const $count = store(0).on(increment, (n, by) => n + by);

const useStoreValue = <T,>(unit: Store<T>): T =>
  useSyncExternalStore((onChange) => watch(unit, onChange), () => unit.getState());

export function Counter() {
  const count = useStoreValue($count);
  return <button onClick={() => increment(1)}>Clicked {count} times</button>;
}
```

Limit: no scope reaches the component this way; scoped rendering (SSR, per-island scopes) waits for `Provider`.

## Never emit

Imports from `react`, `effector-react`, `effector-vue`, `effector-solid` or `@fiberfx/hypergraph/hyperscript` (not exported yet); `useStore`, `useStoreMap`, `useList`, `useGate`.

- [Read this page in the browser](/hypergraph/coming-from-effector/frameworks)

- [All English companions](/llms-full.txt)
- [Sitemap](/sitemap.xml)
- [Course companion](/hypergraph/llms.txt)

# Content, Mercury's page documents — Mercury LMS

> `@fiberfx/schema` 4.0.0 holds the page document format and `parseDocument`; `@fiberfx/content` 4.0.0 holds the block catalog and `renderDocument`. A page is JSON data: parse it against a schema registry, render it through a renderer registry, mount the element.

## Read this when

You show, check or produce a Mercury page document, or you need to know which package owns which step. This page is the course's landing.

## The contract

- `@fiberfx/schema`: `parseDocument(input, registry)` → `{ ok: true, document }` or a refusal `{ ok: false, code, path, reason, subject, node? }`. Also `createSchemaRegistry`, `DEFAULT_LIMITS`, `FORMAT_VERSION`, `applyCommand`, `validateCommand`, `migrateDocument`, `inspectDocument`, `resolveReferences`, `resolveResponsive`.
- `@fiberfx/content`: `renderDocument(document, options)` → `{ element, report }`; `contentRegistry()` (every catalog block), `contentSchema()` (the schema registry content documents validate against), `CATALOG`, `catalogEntries()`, `exampleDocument(entry)`, `createRendererRegistry`, `schemaFor`, `BREAKPOINTS`.
- Peer dependencies of `@fiberfx/content`: `@fiberfx/hyperscript`, `@fiberfx/schema`, `@fiberfx/ui`, each 4.0.0.
- Order: `parseDocument` first, then `renderDocument` on `parsed.document`, then `render(element, container)` from `@fiberfx/hyperscript`.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { render } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript";
import { parseDocument } from "@fiberfx/schema";
import { contentSchema, renderDocument } from "@fiberfx/content";

const main = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("[data-page]");
const response = await fetch("/page.json", { headers: { accept: "application/json" } });
const parsed = parseDocument(await response.text(), contentSchema());
if (main && parsed.ok) {
  const { element } = renderDocument(parsed.document, { mode: "publication", revision: 0 });
  render(element, main);
}
```

## Never emit

A function, an element or a DOM handle inside a document's props: a document is JSON data only. A `renderDocument` call on input that `parseDocument` has not accepted.

# Page documents: nodes, the schema and parseDocument — Mercury LMS

> A Mercury page document (`@fiberfx/schema` 4.0.0) is JSON: `format`, `id`, `kind`, ordered `roots` and a flat `nodes` record. `parseDocument(input, registry)` answers `{ ok: true, document }` or exactly one refusal, and never throws.

## Read this when

You write, generate or store a page document, build a schema registry, or handle a refused document.

## The contract

- Document: `{ format: 1, id: string, kind: "page" | "fragment" | "template", roots: NodeId[], nodes: { [id]: DocumentNode } }`. Unknown fields are kept; they must be JSON.
- Node: `{ id, type, version, props, slots }`. `id` equals its key in `nodes`. `version` is an integer from 1. `props` is JSON only. `slots` maps a slot name to an ordered list of child ids.
- Reference in a prop: `{ "$ref": "asset" | "route" | "entity" | "fragment", "id": string }`; resolved outside the document.
- `createSchemaRegistry({ blocks, limits?, breakpoints?, tokens? })`. Throws `TypeError` on a duplicate type, a version below 1, a migration gap, or defaults failing their schema.
- `BlockDefinition`: `{ type, version, props, defaults?, slots?, migrations? }`. Prop kinds: `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `reference`, `token`, `list`, `record`, `json`; each may be `optional` or `responsive`. Slot: `{ allow?, min?, max? }`.
- `DEFAULT_LIMITS`: `maxDepth` 32, `maxBytes` 1048576 (compact JSON), `maxNodes` 10000, `maxPropDepth` 16.
- Catalog documents: `parseDocument(input, contentSchema())` with `contentSchema` from `@fiberfx/content`; breakpoints `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`.
- `parseDocument(input: unknown, registry)` → `{ ok: true, document }` (the input itself, nothing coerced or defaulted) or `{ ok: false, code, path, reason, subject: "document", node? }`.
- Check order, first failure wins: shape (`malformed`, `newer-format`, `too-many-nodes`, `not-json-safe`, `too-deep`) → size (`too-large`) → structure (`unknown-child`, `multiple-parents`, `cycle`, `too-deep`, `orphan`) → each known node (`unknown-slot`, `slot-cardinality`, `slot-not-allowed`, `unknown-prop`, `missing-prop`, `invalid-prop`) → a fragment referencing itself (`cycle`).
- Unknown block type or newer version: kept and not checked against a definition. Older version: `outdated-block`; migrate first.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { parseDocument } from "@fiberfx/schema";
import { contentSchema } from "@fiberfx/content";

const parsed = parseDocument(
  {
    format: 1,
    id: "hello",
    kind: "page",
    roots: ["page"],
    nodes: {
      page: { id: "page", type: "page", version: 1, props: { title: "Hello" }, slots: { content: ["intro"] } },
      intro: { id: "intro", type: "paragraph", version: 1, props: { text: "A first page." }, slots: {} },
    },
  },
  contentSchema(),
);
if (!parsed.ok) console.log(parsed.code, parsed.path, parsed.reason);
```

## Never emit

A nested node tree inside `props` or `slots`: children are ids in slots. A function, an element or a DOM handle in props. A `try`/`catch` around `parseDocument` in place of checking `parsed.ok`.

# Rendering a document: renderDocument — Mercury LMS

> `renderDocument(document, options)` from `@fiberfx/content` 4.0.0 turns a parsed page document into `{ element, report }`: one `@fiberfx/hyperscript` VNode and the list of unsupported blocks. No fetch, no storage, no provider; preview and publication give the same markup.

## Read this when

You show a page document, choose its render options, pass what the host resolved, or decide whether a page with unknown blocks may publish.

## The contract

- `renderDocument(document: MercuryDocument, options: RenderOptions): { element: VNode, report: { unsupported: NodeId[], publishable: boolean } }`. Pass `parsed.document` from `parseDocument`; it does not validate.
- Required: `mode: "preview" | "publication"` (no block sees it; markup never depends on it), `revision: number` (written as `data-revision`).
- Optional: `theme: "light" | "dark"` (default `light`), `lang`, `dir: "ltr" | "rtl"`, `registry` (default `contentRegistry()`), `resolved: { ["<kind>:<id>"]: { src?, href?, title?, items?, error? } }`, `capabilities: ("embed" | "form")[]` (default none), `allowUnsupported` (default `true`).
- Root: `<div class="mx-content light-theme|dark-theme" data-document=<id> data-revision=<revision> lang dir>`.
- Blocks get `{ node, props, context }`: `props` with responsive values at their base; `node.props` keeps overrides; `context` is `{ theme, capabilities, resolve, slot }`.
- Unregistered type: `<div class="mx-content-unsupported" data-unsupported=<type> role="note">` with "This content can't be shown here." and its slots rendered inside; its id joins `report.unsupported` in document order.
- `report.publishable` is `false` only when something is unsupported and `allowUnsupported: false`.
- Mount with `render(element, container)` from `@fiberfx/hyperscript`.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { render } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript";
import { parseDocument } from "@fiberfx/schema";
import { contentSchema, renderDocument } from "@fiberfx/content";

const main = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("[data-page]");
const response = await fetch("/page.json", { headers: { accept: "application/json" } });
const parsed = parseDocument(await response.text(), contentSchema());
if (main && parsed.ok) {
  const { element, report } = renderDocument(parsed.document, { mode: "publication", revision: 0, lang: "en", theme: "light" });
  render(element, main);
  if (report.unsupported.length > 0) main.dataset.unsupported = String(report.unsupported.length);
}
```

## Never emit

A `fetch` inside a block for its data: pass the host's answers in `resolved`. A branch on `mode` inside a block: blocks can't see it. A `throw` for an unsupported block: it is reported, not an error.

# The block catalog: nine groups, one registry — Mercury LMS

> `@fiberfx/content` 4.0.0's catalog: 51 blocks in nine groups plus the internal `column`, all in `contentRegistry()`. Each entry declares a block `type`, a schema, its host capabilities (`embed`, `form` or none), a renderer and an example.

## Read this when

You write a node of a given block type, need a block's props and slots, or need to know what a block renders and what it asks of the host.

## The contract

- `CATALOG`: `{ group, names }[]`, nine groups, 51 names. `catalogEntries()`: every `BlockEntry` (adds `Column`, group `Internal`). `exampleDocument(entry)`: a one-block page document from the entry's example.
- `BlockEntry`: `{ name, group, type, definition, capabilities, render, example }`.
- Types by group (`?` optional prop):
  - Structure: `page` {title; slot content}, `section` {background? default|muted|primary, responsive; content}, `container` {size? sm–xl; content}, `columns` {count 2–4, reverse? responsive; columns: only `column`, 2–4}, `grid` {cols 1–6; items}, `stack` {gap? sm–xl; content}, `divider` {label?}, `spacer` {size sm–xl}, internal `column` {content}.
  - Text: `heading` {text, level 1–6, size? 1–9}, `paragraph` {text}, `rich-text` {content: [{text, marks? strong|em|code, href?}] ≤500}, `list` {items ≤200, ordered?}, `quote` {text, cite?}, `code` {code, language?}.
  - Media: `image` {asset ref, alt}, `figure` {asset, alt, caption}, `gallery` {images ≤48 [{asset, alt}]}, `video` {title, asset, captions? asset, transcript?}, `audio` {title, asset, transcript?}, `embed` {url, title} (capability `embed`).
  - Navigation: `site-header` {brand; navigation: only `navigation`, ≤1}, `navigation` {label, links ≤40 [{label, href}]}, `breadcrumbs` {items ≤12 [{label, href?}]}, `footer` {text?; content}, `anchor-links` {label, links ≤40 [{label, target}]}.
  - Composition: `button` {label, href, variant? primary|secondary|ghost}, `button-group` {buttons: only `button`, 1–4}, `hero` {title, subtitle?; actions: button|button-group ≤1}, `cta-section` {title, text?; actions}, `card` {title, text?, href?}, `card-grid` {columns? 1–4; cards: only `card`}, `feature-list` {items ≤24 [{title, text}]}, `logo-list` {label, logos ≤24 [{name, asset?}]}, `testimonials` {items ≤24 [{quote, author, role?}]}.
  - Interactive content: `accordion` {items ≤30 [{title, text}]}, `tabs` {label?, items ≤12 [{label, text}]}, `disclosure` {summary, text}, `carousel` {label?, autoAdvance?, slides ≤20 [{text}]}.
  - Form content: `form` {label, action route ref; fields} (capability `form`), `field-group` {legend; fields}, `field` {kind text|email|tel|number|url|textarea|checkbox|select, name, label, required?, options? ≤50}, `form-submit` {label, success?, error?, state? idle|success|error} (capability `form`).
  - Data-backed content: `collection-feed`, `article-list`, `related-content` {title, collection entity ref}; `author-card` {name, bio?, href?}.
  - Editorial page: `article-header` {title, subtitle?, author?, published?}, `article-body` {content}, `table-of-contents` {label?, items ≤50 [{label, target}]}, `metadata` {items ≤20 [{label, value}]}, `related-articles` {title, collection entity ref}.
- Behaviour: images and media never fetch; an unresolved image shows its alt as `role="img"`. `embed` frames only absolute https with the `embed` capability, `sandbox="allow-scripts"`; else a link. Every panel and slide is in static markup; Tabs and Carousel upgrade once mounted. A form posts natively only with `form` granted and a resolved route; else it is disabled and says so. Data-backed blocks render `data-state` `error`, `unavailable`, `empty` or `ready` from the host's snapshot. Author hrefs pass `safeHref`: relative, `#`, `?`, http, https, mailto, tel; anything else renders with no href.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { catalogEntries, contentSchema, exampleDocument, renderDocument } from "@fiberfx/content";
import { parseDocument } from "@fiberfx/schema";

for (const entry of catalogEntries().filter((entry) => entry.group !== "Internal")) {
  const parsed = parseDocument(exampleDocument(entry), contentSchema());
  if (!parsed.ok) throw new Error(`${entry.name}: ${parsed.code} at ${parsed.path}`);
  const { report } = renderDocument(parsed.document, { mode: "preview", revision: 1 });
  console.log(entry.group, entry.name, entry.type, report.unsupported.length);
}
```

## Never emit

A catalog name as a node's `type` (`"RichText display"`): documents use the type (`"rich-text"`). Raw HTML in a rich-text run. A `level` chosen for its visual size: set `size` instead. A child whose type a slot's `allow` excludes (`slot-not-allowed`).

# References, capabilities and responsive values — Mercury LMS

> What `renderDocument` (`@fiberfx/content` 4.0.0) leaves to the host: a `resolved` record keyed `<kind>:<id>` for every reference, the `embed` and `form` capabilities, and responsive props read at their base. Blocks never fetch, and every missing answer has a visible fallback.

## Read this when

You host Mercury pages and must supply images, routes or collections, grant or withhold embeds and forms, or read a responsive prop at a breakpoint.

## The contract

- Reference in a prop: `{ $ref: "asset" | "route" | "entity" | "fragment", id }`. Key: `referenceKey(reference)` → `"<$ref>:<id>"` (`@fiberfx/schema`).
- `renderDocument(document, { resolved })`: `resolved: { [key]: { src?, href?, title?, items?: { title, href?, summary? }[], error? } }`. Nothing in the package fetches.
- Readers: `image`/`figure`/`gallery`/`logo-list`/`audio` read `src`; `video` reads `src` for its asset and `captions`; `form` reads `href` (with `form` granted); `collection-feed`/`article-list`/`related-content`/`related-articles` read `items` and `error`. No catalog block reads `title`.
- Data-backed states: key missing → `unavailable`; `items: []` → `empty`; `error` → `error` (alert); items → `ready`.
- `@fiberfx/schema`: `collectReferences(document)` → `{ node, path, reference }[]`; `resolveReferences(document, resolve)` → `Map<key, { status: "resolved" | "unknown" | "unauthorized", reference, details? }>`, once per key; `unauthorized` keeps only the identity; any other answer throws `TypeError`. Converting a `Resolution` to `resolved` is the host's job.
- `capabilities: ("embed" | "form")[]`, none by default. `renderDocument` does not enforce an entry's declared capabilities; each block reads `context.capabilities`.
- `embed`: an `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts">` only with `embed` granted and an absolute https URL; else a link. `form`: posts only with `form` granted and a safe resolved `href`; else disabled, with "This form can't be sent from here." `form-submit`: disabled without `form`.
- Author `href`s kept: `/`, `./`, `../`, `#`, `?`, `http:`, `https:`, `mailto:`, `tel:`. Dropped (label kept, no href): other schemes, `//`, `/\`, `\\`, any control character. `safeHref` and `httpsUrl` are not exported.
- Responsive value: `{ $responsive: { base?, overrides: { [breakpoint]: value | { $removed: true } } } }`, only on props with `responsive: true` (catalog: `section.background`, `columns.reverse`). `BREAKPOINTS` = `["sm", "md", "lg", "xl"]`. An override at another name, or a wrapper on a non-responsive prop: `invalid-prop`.
- Blocks get the base in `props`; `node.props` keeps overrides. `section` renders the base only. `columns` writes `data-reverse` / `data-reverse-<bp>`, and no stylesheet in the repository reads them.
- `resolveResponsive(value, breakpoint, BREAKPOINTS)` → `{ state: "explicit" | "inherited" | "removed" | "absent", from?, value? }`.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { renderDocument, type ResolvedReference } from "@fiberfx/content";
import { collectReferences, referenceKey, type MercuryDocument } from "@fiberfx/schema";

function show(document: MercuryDocument, sources: { readonly [id: string]: string }) {
  const resolved: { [key: string]: ResolvedReference } = {};
  for (const { reference } of collectReferences(document)) {
    const src = reference.$ref === "asset" ? sources[reference.id] : undefined;
    if (src !== undefined) resolved[referenceKey(reference)] = { src };
  }
  return renderDocument(document, { mode: "publication", revision: 0, resolved, capabilities: ["embed"] });
}
```

## Never emit

A `fetch` inside a block to resolve a reference. A resolved key without its kind (`"hero"` for `"asset:hero"`). An `import { safeHref } from "@fiberfx/content"`: it is not exported. A responsive wrapper on a prop whose schema isn't `responsive`.

# Add a block: the capstone — Mercury LMS

> Add your own block to Mercury page documents (`@fiberfx/content` 4.0.0): write a `BlockEntry`, put it in a registry with `createRendererRegistry([...catalogEntries(), entry])`, derive its schema with `schemaFor(registry)`, then parse and render `exampleDocument(entry)` with both.

## Read this when

You need a block the catalog doesn't have, or you are checking a block entry before a page uses it.

## The contract

- `BlockEntry`: `{ name, group, type, definition, capabilities, render, example }`. `group` is a catalog group or `"Internal"` (closed union). `definition.type` must equal `type`. `capabilities`: `[]`, `["embed"]` or `["form"]`.
- `render({ node, props, context })`: `props` at their base; `context` is `{ theme, capabilities, resolve, slot }`, never the mode. `.tsx` with `jsxImportSource: "@fiberfx/hyperscript"`.
- `example`: `{ props, slots?: { [slot]: { type, props, slots? }[] } }`.
- `createRendererRegistry(entries)` throws `Error` for a type registered twice (`block type "x" is registered twice`) or a type mismatch (`"Name" declares type "a" but its definition is "b"`).
- `schemaFor(registry)` → the schema registry (every definition, `BREAKPOINTS`). It throws `TypeError` for a version below 1, a migration gap, failing defaults, an unknown prop kind, or any `token` prop (no token sets are declared).
- Parse your documents with `schemaFor(registry)`. Under `contentSchema()` your type is unknown, so it is kept and unchecked. Render with `{ registry }`, or your node is unsupported.
- The example check: parse `exampleDocument(entry)`, render it, and expect non-empty markup with `report.unsupported` empty. `exampleDocument` takes versions from `contentRegistry()`, else 1, so keep a new block at version 1.
- `safeHref` and `httpsUrl` are not exported; check author links yourself. Declared capabilities aren't enforced; read `context.capabilities`.

## Minimal example

```tsx
import { parseDocument } from "@fiberfx/schema";
import { catalogEntries, createRendererRegistry, exampleDocument, renderDocument, schemaFor, type BlockEntry } from "@fiberfx/content";

const callout: BlockEntry = {
  name: "Callout",
  group: "Composition",
  type: "callout",
  definition: { type: "callout", version: 1, props: { title: { kind: "string", maxLength: 120 } }, slots: { content: {} } },
  capabilities: [],
  render: ({ node, props, context }) => (
    <aside class="callout" role="note">
      <p>{typeof props.title === "string" ? props.title : ""}</p>
      {context.slot(node, "content")}
    </aside>
  ),
  example: { props: { title: "Before you start" }, slots: { content: [{ type: "paragraph", props: { text: "Inside." } }] } },
};

const registry = createRendererRegistry([...catalogEntries(), callout]);
const parsed = parseDocument(exampleDocument(callout), schemaFor(registry));
if (!parsed.ok) throw new Error(`${parsed.code} at ${parsed.path}`);
const { report } = renderDocument(parsed.document, { mode: "preview", revision: 1, registry });
if (report.unsupported.length > 0) throw new Error("callout is unsupported");
```

## Never emit

A `group` outside the catalog's nine or `"Internal"`. A `definition.type` that differs from `type`. A `token` prop with `schemaFor`. A parse against `contentSchema()` for a document using your block. A `renderDocument` call without `registry` for one.

# Live Mercury, islands on the BEAM — Mercury LMS

> Mercury hyperscript components ("islands") inside Phoenix and LiveView. Server: `LiveMercury.mercury/1` (echo/apps/live_mercury). Browser: `@fiberfx/live-mercury` 4.0.0, peer `@fiberfx/hyperscript`. EDU's islands are built by `mx build --lib` with no Node.

## Read this when

You put a Mercury component on a page Phoenix renders, wire it to a LiveView, or build its bundle. This is the course's landing; LM0–LM5 follow, and LM6 is planned.

## The contract

- An island is one element with `phx-update="ignore"` and a `phx-hook`; a client hook mounts a hyperscript component into it.
- Server, LiveView host: `<LiveMercury.mercury name="X" ...props />` renders `phx-hook="MercuryHook"`, `data-name="X"`, `data-props`, `data-props-diff`, `data-streams-diff`, `data-slots`, `data-ssr`, `data-use-diff`.
- Browser: `getHooks({ X })` returns `{ MercuryHook }` for `new LiveSocket(path, Socket, { hooks })`. The server's `name` must equal the map's key.
- EDU host: `<.island id bundle props>` (`EchoEduWeb.Island`) renders `phx-hook="CourseIsland"`, `data-bundle`, and a `<script type="application/json">` props child. The bundle exports `default` and `hook = courseIsland(Component)` from `@echd/edu-boot/island`.
- `@fiberfx/live-mercury` exports: `getHooks`, `createMercuryHook`, `useLiveMercury`, `LiveMercuryProvider`, `LiveMercuryContext`, `Link`, `decodeCompactJson`, `decodeCompactPatch`, `applyPatch`, `applyOperation`, `getValueByPointer`.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { Socket } from "@fiberfx/phoenix";
import { LiveSocket } from "@fiberfx/phoenix_live_view";
import { getHooks } from "@fiberfx/live-mercury";
import { KanBoard } from "./board";

const liveSocket = new LiveSocket("/live", Socket, { hooks: getHooks({ KanBoard }) as never });
liveSocket.connect();
```

## Never emit

An import from `react` or `react-dom`. Islands render with `@fiberfx/hyperscript`.

## Limits

- EDU's islands are built by mx in the image (no `node` in that stage). The KAN views' `kan.mjs` is committed and built outside the image.

<!-- /live-mercury/islands/llms.txt -->

# Islands: the element and its mount — Mercury LMS

> LM0. An island is one server-rendered element with `phx-update="ignore"` and a `phx-hook`, into which a Mercury hyperscript component mounts. Two hosts: `LiveMercury.mercury/1` (hook `MercuryHook`, component by name) and `EchoEduWeb.Island.island/1` (hook `CourseIsland`, component by bundle URL).

## Read this when

You render an island from HEEx, register its component on the client, or debug an island that does not mount.

## The contract

- `<.mercury name="X" ...>` (`import LiveMercury`). Reserved assigns: `name` (required), `id` (default `"X-<n>"`, per-process counter), `class`, `ssr` (default `config :live_mercury, :ssr`, `false`), `diff` (default `:enable_props_diff`, `true`), `socket` (only decides the first render is dead). Every other assign is a prop; a `%Phoenix.LiveView.LiveStream{}` assign is a stream; the default `:inner_block` slot becomes `children`. Props encode via the `LiveMercury.Encoder` protocol.
- Element attributes: `data-name`, `data-props` (compact JSON), `data-props-diff`, `data-use-diff`, `data-streams-diff`, `data-slots` (base64 default slot), `data-ssr`, `phx-update="ignore"`, `phx-hook="MercuryHook"`.
- Client: `getHooks(components)` → `{ MercuryHook }`; `createMercuryHook(resolve)` takes `el => Component | Promise<Component>`. The component gets `{...props, ...streams, pushEvent, pushEventTo, handleEvent, removeHandleEvent, upload, uploadTo}` and the slot as a child, inside `LiveMercuryProvider`. With `data-ssr`, the first paint clears the server markup (no hydration).
- EDU: `<.island id bundle props>`; `id` and `bundle` required, `props` a map (default `%{}`), slot = the server render, kept until mount and restored at `destroyed`. Props go in a `<script type="application/json">` first child, `<` written as `\u003c`. URL: `EchoEduWeb.Island.bundle_url(name)` → `/_edu/assets/edu-island-<name>.js`.
- An EDU bundle exports `default` (its component) and `hook = courseIsland(Component)` from `@echd/edu-boot/island`. Its component also gets `islandId`, the element's id; EDU's props win over Live Mercury's keys.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { courseIsland } from "@echd/edu-boot/island";
import { DemoIsland } from "./DemoIsland";

export default DemoIsland;
export const hook = courseIsland(DemoIsland);
```

## Errors

- `MercuryHook` throws when the element has no `data-name`, or when `getHooks`'s map has no component of that name.
- `CourseIsland` writes `data-island-error`: `no-bundle`, `import`, `no-hook`, `props` (JSON child does not parse), `render` (the bundle's `mounted` threw). Success sets `data-island-mounted="true"`.
- Build time: `EchoEduWeb.Island.check_hosts/3` (run by `mix edu.gen`) refuses a `CourseIsland` host outside the body, without a unique id, without `phx-update="ignore"`, with a `data-bundle` that is not a path or http(s) URL, or without a parsing JSON first child.

## Never emit

`phx-hook="ReactHook"`, or an import from `react`. A `<.mercury>` without `name`.

<!-- /live-mercury/liveview/llms.txt -->

# An island in a LiveView: socket, hooks and events — Mercury LMS

> LM1. One LiveSocket per page; `MercuryHook`'s `mounted`/`updated`/`reconnected`/`destroyed`; props that follow the LiveView's assigns as patches; events up with `pushEvent` and down with `push_event` + `handleEvent`.

## Read this when

You connect an island to its LiveView: open the socket, send an event from the island, answer it on the server, or push a server event to one island.

## The contract

- Socket paths: echd_os `socket "/live"`; echo_edu `socket "/_edu/live"`, read by EDU's boot from `<meta name="edu-live-socket">` (else `"/live"`).
- One LiveSocket per page: `new LiveSocket(path, Socket, { params: { _csrf_token }, hooks })`. The import map points `@fiberfx/phoenix` and `@fiberfx/phoenix_live_view` at one served copy each.
- `updated()`: `data-use-diff="true"` → `applyPatch(props, data-props-diff)`, else full `data-props`; streams patched from `data-streams-diff`. `reconnected()`: full `data-props`, streams rebuilt from `{}`. `destroyed()`: `render(null)` and every `handleEvent` ref made through the hook removed.
- Each update publishes a new top-level props object; untouched nested values keep identity.
- Server side, `diff` on (default): only assigns LiveView marks changed are sent; a key with no old value → `replace /<key>`, else `Jsonpatch.diff` under `/<key>`.
- Hook functions (props, or `useLiveMercury()`; `null` outside an island): `pushEvent(event, payload?, onReply?)`, `pushEventTo(phxTarget, event, payload?, onReply?)`, `handleEvent(event, cb)` → ref, `removeHandleEvent(ref)`, `upload(name, files)`, `uploadTo(target, name, files)`.
- EDU server events: one name, `"edu:island"` (`SERVER_EVENT`), envelope `%{id, event, payload}`; filter with `isAddressedTo(payload, islandId)` from `@echd/edu-boot/island`.
- `Link`: `patch` → `data-phx-link="patch"`; `navigate` → `"redirect"` (same `live_session`); `replace` → `data-phx-link-state="replace"`; `href` alone → plain link.

## Minimal example

```tsx
import { useEffect } from "@fiberfx/hyperscript/hooks";
import { useLiveMercury } from "@fiberfx/live-mercury";
import { isAddressedTo, SERVER_EVENT } from "@echd/edu-boot/island";

export function Ping(props: { islandId?: string }) {
  const live = useLiveMercury();
  const handleEvent = live?.handleEvent;
  const removeHandleEvent = live?.removeHandleEvent;
  const islandId = props.islandId ?? "";
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!handleEvent || !removeHandleEvent) return;
    const ref = handleEvent(SERVER_EVENT, (payload) => {
      if (isAddressedTo(payload, islandId)) console.log(payload.event, payload.payload);
    });
    return () => removeHandleEvent(ref);
  }, [handleEvent, removeHandleEvent, islandId]);
  return <button type="button" onClick={() => live?.pushEvent("demo:clicked", { count: 1 })}>Ping</button>;
}
```

```elixir
def handle_event("demo:clicked", %{"count" => count}, socket) do
  {:noreply, push_event(socket, "edu:island", %{id: "island-demo", event: "ack", payload: %{count: count}})}
end
```

## Never emit

A second `new LiveSocket(...)` on a page that already has one; `phx-update` other than `"ignore"` on an island; an import from `react`.
