# Building islands with mx: no Node — Mercury LMS

> LM2. `mx build --lib` bundles one entry into one ES module (Rolldown, Hypercompiler, no sid). EDU's five island assets are five such builds; the echd-os image runs them in a stage with no `node` on PATH.

## Read this when

You build an island bundle, add an island to EDU, or change how the image builds islands.

## The contract

- `mx build --lib <entry> --out <file> [--root <dir>] [--external <package>]... [--define <name>=<expression>]... [--minify] [--require-export <name>]...`. `--lib` and `--out` are required; `--root` defaults to `.`; any other flag is refused; `--lib` cannot combine with `--bundle` or `--host`.
- Imports resolve from members' source, as under `mx dev`. An `--external` package (and its subpaths) stays a bare import for the page's import map. A CSS import becomes an empty module; nothing is written for it.
- One output file: more than one chunk is an error. `--require-export` missing → exit 1, `"<entry> does not export <names> (it exports …)"`, nothing written.
- An island's `mx.mod` lists every module its import graph reaches (`require`) and each one's directory (`replace`).
- EDU's builds (`node/apps/edu-boot/bin/build-assets.sh <dest>`, `MX` = mx binary): `phoenix.js`; `phoenix_live_view.js` (`--external @fiberfx/phoenix`, `--define LV_VSN=…`); `edu-boot.js` (phoenix pair + `phoenix` external); `edu-island-demo.js` (`--require-export default --require-export hook`); `edu-island-kan.js` (also `--require-export KanFigure`). All `--minify`. Islands have no externals.
- `scripts/edu/build-islands.sh` writes them to `echo/apps/echo_edu/priv/static/edu` (ignored, never committed), adds `mercury.css` and fonts, and fails if any of six files is missing or empty. Served at `/_edu/assets`.
- Image (`echo/Dockerfile`, stage `edu-islands`, `rust:1.97.0-bookworm`): `cargo build --release --locked --bin mx`, then `! command -v node && MX=… bash scripts/edu/build-islands.sh`; the Elixir stage copies `priv/static/edu` in before `mix release echd_os`.

## Minimal example

```sh
mx build --lib node/apps/edu-island-demo/src/index.tsx --root node/apps/edu-island-demo \
  --out priv/static/edu/edu-island-demo.js --minify --require-export default --require-export hook
```

## Limits

- echd_os's `kan.mjs` (the KAN views' islands) is committed and built by `node/apps/echd-os/bin/kan-build.sh` with pnpm, tsc, Vitest and Vite; the image builds no JavaScript for it.
- Development: `EDU_ISLAND_DEV` (`name=url,…`) can point `bundle_url(name)` at a Vite dev server's `.ts`/`.tsx` entry; the boot installs Vite's HMR client first.
- The runtime image is `node:<version>-bookworm-slim`; its `node` is for a forthcoming worker, not a build step.

<!-- /live-mercury/props-and-streams/llms.txt -->

# Props and streams: patches on the wire — Mercury LMS

> LM3. After the first render, `LiveMercury.mercury/1` sends changed props as a JSON Patch in `data-props-diff` and LiveView streams as patches in `data-streams-diff`, both in a compact wire format. `@fiberfx/live-mercury` decodes them with `decodeCompactPatch` and applies them with `applyPatch`, which adds `upsert`, `limit` and `$$<id>` paths to RFC 6902.

## Read this when

You debug an island that shows stale props, render a LiveView stream in an island, or decode or apply Live Mercury's patches yourself.

## The contract

- `data-props`: full props, compact JSON; sent on the first render, a dead render, or with `diff={false}`. `data-props-diff`: sent on later renders with `diff` on (default `config :live_mercury, :enable_props_diff`, `true`, compile time). A connected re-render with `diff` on does not resend `data-props`.
- Client `updated()`: `data-use-diff="true"` → `applyPatch(props, decodeCompactPatch(data-props-diff))`; else full `data-props`. Streams: always `applyPatch(streams, decodeCompactPatch(data-streams-diff))`.
- Props diff: changed key with no old value → `replace /<key>`; with an old value → `Jsonpatch.diff` under `/<key>` (structs via `LiveMercury.Encoder`, list items matched by `id`). Every diff starts with a root `test` nonce, serialized `n<digits>`, skipped by the decoder.
- Streams (`%Phoenix.LiveView.LiveStream{}` assigns, never props): reset → `replace /<name> []`; delete → `remove /<name>/$$<dom_id>`; insert → `upsert /<name>/-` (at -1) or `/<name>/<at>`; update only → `replace /<name>/$$<dom_id>`; limit → `limit /<name> <n>`. Items carry `__dom_id`. First and dead renders reset every stream first.
- Wire: `<op><path_len>:<path><value>`; ops `a` add, `d` remove (no value), `r` replace, `u` upsert, `l` limit; values `z`, `b0`/`b1`, `n<len>:<num>`, `s<len>:<str>`, `J<len>:<compact json>`. Lengths are JavaScript string lengths (UTF-16 units).
- Compact JSON: `"` → `^`, `^` → `~^`, `~` → `~~`. `decodeCompactJson` reverses it.
- `applyPatch(doc, ops)`: copy on write below the root (each touched container cloned once per batch); the root is mutated and returned. `applyOperation(doc, op)`: one op in place. `getValueByPointer(doc, pointer)`.
- `$$<id>`: the item whose `__dom_id` loosely equals `id`; missing → warning, op skipped. `upsert`: replace by `__dom_id`, else insert. `limit n`: keep first `n` (n ≥ 0) or last `|n|` (n < 0). `test`: no-op.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { applyPatch, decodeCompactPatch } from "@fiberfx/live-mercury";

const props = { count: 5, items: ["a", "b", "c"] };
const next = applyPatch(props, decodeCompactPatch("n123r6:/countn1:6d8:/items/0"));
// next === props; next.count === 6; next.items is a new array ["b", "c"]
```

## Errors

`decodeCompactPatch` throws `Unknown LiveMercury patch operation code`, `Unknown LiveMercury patch value tag`, or `Invalid LiveMercury patch length prefix`. A props struct without `LiveMercury.Encoder` raises `Protocol.UndefinedError`.

## Never emit

A `move` or `copy` operation: neither has an op code in the wire format. Byte lengths in a hand-written payload.

<!-- /live-mercury/server-rendering/llms.txt -->

# Server rendering: what is there, and what is not — Mercury LMS

> LM4. `<.mercury ssr={true}>` asks the configured `LiveMercury.SSR` module for an island's HTML on the first, dead render. No module is configured anywhere in the umbrella, SSR is off by default, a `<.mercury>` element starts empty, and the client replaces server markup instead of hydrating it.

## Read this when

You are asked to server-render an island, see an empty island element before JavaScript runs, or see `data-ssr` on an element.

## The contract

- `ssr` assign; default `config :live_mercury, :ssr` (compile time), `false`. Applies only when `__changed__` is `nil` and the socket is not connected (the dead first render).
- On: `LiveMercury.SSR.render(name, encoded_props, slots)`. Raises `LiveMercury.SSR.NotConfigured` → treated as off. Otherwise the element gets `data-ssr` and the response's `:html` as content.
- `LiveMercury.SSR` behaviour: `@callback render(component_name, props, slots) :: render_response | no_return`. Configure with `config :live_mercury, ssr_module: Mod`. Telemetry span `[:live_mercury, :ssr]`, metadata `%{component, props, slots}`. A binary response splits at `<!-- preload -->` into `preloadLinks` (unused by the template) and `html`.
- With no `:ssr_module`, `render/3` returns `%{preloadLinks: "", html: ""}`: `ssr={true}` gives `data-ssr` around empty HTML (tested).
- With SSR off, a `<.mercury>` element starts empty; props are in `data-props`, the default slot base64 in `data-slots`, rendered by the client.
- Client: with `data-ssr`, the first paint clears the element, then renders. No hydration. Without `data-ssr`, existing children are kept.
- `LiveMercury.SSR.ViteJS` (POST `{:vite_host}/ssr_render`) and `LiveMercury.SSR.NodeJS` (a `server.js` via the `NodeJS` package) exist, are not configured here, and need a JavaScript runtime.
- EDU's `<.island>` inner block is a hand-written no-JS fallback, set aside while the island lives and restored after. It is not SSR.

## Minimal example

```elixir
def ssr_on_component(assigns) do
  ~H"""
  <.mercury name="MyComponent" ssr={true} />
  """
end

# with no :ssr_module configured: data-ssr is set, the element's HTML is empty
assert LiveMercury.Test.get_mercury(render_component(&ssr_on_component/1)).ssr == true
```

## Never emit

`config :live_mercury, ssr: true` without a renderer that returns real HTML; a claim that an island is hydrated; `hydrate` or `hydrateRoot` calls in an island bundle expecting Live Mercury to use them.

<!-- /live-mercury/testing/llms.txt -->

# Testing islands: both sides of the element — Mercury LMS

> LM5. Server: `LiveMercury.Test.get_mercury/2` decodes a `<.mercury>` element; `Phoenix.LiveViewTest`'s `render_hook/3` and `assert_push_event/3` test an island's events. Client: `MercuryHook` driven on a stand-in hook under Vitest. EDU: ConnCase page tests, `courseIsland` and boot tests, built-bundle checks, a headless-Chrome page check, and `check_hosts/3` at generation time.

## Read this when

You write a test for an island, its LiveView, or an EDU course page that hosts one.

## The contract

- `LiveMercury.Test.get_mercury(view | html, opts \\ [])`; a `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.View` is rendered first. Needs `{:floki, ">= 0.30.0", only: :test}`. Finds `[phx-hook='MercuryHook']` elements only.
- Returns `%{component, id, props, props_diff, streams_diff, slots, ssr, use_diff, class}`. `props_diff`/`streams_diff`: lists `[op, path]` (remove) or `[op, path, value]`; nonce dropped. `slots`: base64-decoded, e.g. `%{"default" => "…"}`. `ssr`: `data-ssr` present.
- Options `name:` / `id:`; no match raises `No Mercury component found with name="…". Available components: Name#id, …`; another option → `ArgumentError`; no island → `No Mercury components found in the rendered HTML`.
- With `diff` on, `:props` after a connected update is still the first snapshot; assert on `:props_diff`, or `config :live_mercury, enable_props_diff: false` in test config (compile time).
- Simulate a re-render: call `LiveMercury.mercury(assigns)` with `__changed__: %{}` and `assign/3`; a connected socket for stream diffs: `%Phoenix.LiveView.Socket{transport_pid: self()}`.
- Events: `render_hook(view, "event", params)` plays the island's `pushEvent`; `assert_push_event(view, "event", payload)` sees what its `handleEvent` would get.
- Hook tests (`fiberfx/live-mercury/src/hooks.test.ts`): `createLiveViewHook(attrs)` (in `src/test/`, not exported) gives a real element and spies; `getHooks({ TestComponent })`; call `definition[step].call(hook)`; change attributes with `el.setAttribute` between `mounted` and `updated`.
- `EchoEduWeb.Island.check_hosts(source, masked, {body_at, body_len})` → `:ok` or `{:error, reason}`: `:no_id`, `{:outside_body, id}`, `{:duplicate_id, id}`, `{:not_ignored, id}`, `{:no_bundle, id}`, `{:bundle, id}`, `{:props, id}`. `EchoEdu.Gen.split/1` wraps it as `{:error, {:island_host, reason}}`.
- Browser: `node scripts/edu/island-check.mjs <page-url> [screenshot.png]` (default the demo page) checks mount, one `/_edu/live` socket, a click round trip, the no-JS render, no errors.

## Minimal example

```elixir
test "renders component with correct props" do
  html = render_component(&simple_component/1)
  island = LiveMercury.Test.get_mercury(html)

  assert island.component == "MyComponent"
  assert island.props == %{"firstName" => "john", "lastName" => "doe"}
end
```

## Never emit

`island.handlers` (documented in `LiveMercury.Test`'s moduledoc but not in the returned map); `get_mercury/2` on an EDU `CourseIsland` page; an assertion on `:props` after an update with diffs on.

## Limits

The hook tests, `island-check.mjs`, `f1-gate.mjs` and the built-bundle rows need Node. Whether the hook tests pass under `mx test` is not recorded. No browser check found for a `<.mercury>` island.

Mercury is maintained by Jonny Novikov. Public contact: mercury@jonnify.com. The official documentation is mercury.jonnify.com; the public distribution repository is https://github.com/fiberfx/mercury. No postal address is published.

# Mercury website privacy

Privacy contact: Jonny Novikov, mercury@jonnify.com. The website can record request information and, when tracking is enabled and permitted, IP, user-agent, referrer, country and visitor/session identifiers. Cookies: theme (one year), _ms_vid (two years), _ms_sid (30 idle minutes); the analytics layer honors _ma_optout=1. Cookie expiry does not establish server retention. Google Fonts and the UNPKG browser example are external resources. Read the full notice before making privacy claims; no server retention duration or postal address is published.

# Mercury API reference

Use this page when looking up the Mercury API or mx CLI. It is an authored reference index, not a generated catalog of every symbol.

- [Hyperscript API](/hyperscript/llms.txt): h, render, JSX and hooks.
- [Mercury UI API](/ui/llms.txt): components and CSS tokens.
- [Hypergraph units](/hypergraph/units/llms.txt): store, event and effect.
- [mx CLI](/mx/llms.txt) and [installation](/start/install-mx/llms.txt).
- [Live Mercury](/live-mercury/llms.txt): optional Phoenix and LiveView integration.
- [Public HTTP API index](/api) and [OpenAPI 3.1 description](/openapi.json): read-only discovery, release metadata and the MCP HTTP boundary.
- [MCP connection guide](/start/mcp/llms.txt): use MCP initialization and discovery; this is JSON-RPC, not a REST substitute. `/api` errors use RFC 9457; MCP errors retain JSON-RPC envelopes.
- [Public distribution repository](https://github.com/fiberfx/mercury).

Use the exact package entry points from each chapter. Preserve existing application pins and check current readiness before installing tools.
